item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to Boost Higher Education Among Scheduled Caste Students
Revised Funding Pattern, Direct Benefit Transfer and End-to-End Online Processing Ensure Greater Transparency and Timely Scholarship Delivery
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students with the objective of significantly increasing the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of SC students in higher education, particularly those belonging to the poorest households. The scheme provides financial assistance at the post-matriculation and post-secondary levels, enabling eligible Scheduled Caste students to pursue and complete their education.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Shri Golla Baburao in Rajya Sabha, informed the House that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme has been implemented continuously in the State of Andhra Pradesh since 2020-21. Scholarships have been disbursed to eligible applicants across all districts of the State.

According to the latest available data, Andhra Pradesh received Central Assistance of ₹149.03 crore, benefiting 81,667 students during 2026-27 (up to 24 July 2026).

The Minister further informed that the funding pattern of the scheme was revised in 2020-21, replacing the earlier concept of State Committed Liability with a fixed Centre-State sharing ratio of 60:40, while the ratio for North-Eastern States has been fixed at 90:10. The revised funding pattern has reduced the financial burden on States and enhanced the Central Government's contribution towards the scheme.

The House was also informed that several transformative reforms have been introduced under the scheme to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability. These include end-to-end online processing of applications, digital verification of eligibility through linkage with available databases, faster verification, continuous monitoring, prevention of duplication and timely delivery of scholarship benefits.

Further, the Government introduced Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the scheme from 2021-22, ensuring that scholarship amounts are transferred directly into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of eligible students. The initiative has simplified the flow of funds, improved transparency and ensured accurate targeting of beneficiaries. Applications are invited through the designated State scholarship portals or the National Scholarship Portal, while the release of the Central share is contingent upon the timely release of the corresponding State share.

The Minister also informed that delays in verification of applications by States and delays in the release of the State share can consequently delay the release of the Central assistance to eligible beneficiaries. The Government continues to work with States and Union Territories to ensure timely verification and disbursement of scholarships so that eligible Scheduled Caste students receive financial assistance without delay.

*******

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Scholarship Delivery Through DBT; Over 47.53 Lakh Post-Matric and 26.79 Lakh Pre-Matric Scholarships Awarded in 2025-26
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) for Scheduled Castes and Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes & Others as Centrally Sponsored Schemes to promote educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste students across the country. The schemes are implemented through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode, ensuring timely, transparent and efficient disbursement of scholarship benefits to eligible students.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in a written reply to Shri Kota Srinivasa Poojary, Shri Tejasvi Sury, Shri Jaswantsinh Sumanbhai Bhabhor, Shri Pradeep Kumar Singh, Shri Bharatsinhji Shankarji Dabhi, Shri Yogender Chandolia, Smt. Kamlesh Jangde, Shri Ramesh Awasthi, Shri Captain Brijesh Chowta, Shri Radheshyam Rathiya, Shri Suresh Kumar Kashyap, Shri Janardan Mishra, Shri Naba Charan Majh, Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Shri Avimanyu Sethi, Shri Bibhu Prasad Tarai, Shri Chavda Vinod Lakhamshi and Shri Khagen Murmu. The House was informed that both scholarship schemes are open-ended and demand-driven, enabling all eligible students enrolled in recognised educational institutions across India to avail scholarship benefits. Annual Action Plans are received from States and Union Territories in accordance with the scheme guidelines.

The written reply further stated that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme follows a funding pattern of 60:40 between the Centre and States and 90:10 for North-Eastern States, while the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme follows a 60:40 funding pattern, 90:10 for North-Eastern States, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, and 100 per cent Central funding for Union Territories without legislatures.

The House was also informed that the Government has introduced several reforms to enhance transparency, accountability and continuous monitoring of the scholarship schemes. Through Aadhaar-enabled Direct Benefit Transfer, scholarship amounts are credited directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts, eliminating leakages, ensuring accurate targeting and enabling faster flow of funds. Applications are processed through designated State Scholarship Portals and the National Scholarship Portal, while verification and approval are undertaken by the respective State Governments and Union Territories as per the scheme guidelines.

According to the data shared in Parliament, during 2025-26, the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme benefited 47,53,420 students across the country, while the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme benefited 26,79,049 students, reaffirming the Government's continued commitment towards expanding educational opportunities for Scheduled Caste students.
The reply further provided district-wise information for Dakshina Kannada (Karnataka), Dahod (Gujarat) and Shimla (Himachal Pradesh).

Between 2022-23 and 2025-26, the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme covered 29,184 beneficiaries with Central Assistance amounting to ₹35.91 crore, while the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme covered 34,184 beneficiaries with Central Assistance of ₹8.15 crore across these districts.

item.content:encoded:
UPSC
INDIAN ECONOMIC SERVICE/INDIAN STATISTICAL SERVICE EXAMINATION 2026
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi

On the basis of the result of the written part of the Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service Examination 2026 held by the UPSC from 19th June to 21st June, 2026, the candidates with the under mentioned Roll Numbers have qualified for Interview/Personality Test.

The candidature of these candidates is PROVISIONAL subject to their being found eligible in all respects. The candidates would be required to produce the original certificates in support of their claims relating to age, educational qualifications, community, benchmark disability (where applicable) etc. at the time of the Personality Test. They are, therefore, advised to keep their certificates ready and check beforehand the requirement of certificates in accordance with the important instructions available on the website of the Commission before appearing in the Personality Test.

The Commission shall provide a window of 15 (Fifteen) days after the declaration of result of written part of Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service (IES/ISS) Examination, 2026. All the candidates, as per Rule 4.1(2) of Rules of IES/ISS Examination, 2026, who qualified for the Personality Test/Interview shall be required to mandatorily login to the portal (https://upsconline.nic.in) during this period and shall be required to update their details/educational qualification status (whether appearing/appeared) alongwith proof of passing the requisite qualifying examination, and upload the relevant documents as proof of their claim, failing which, such candidates will not be allowed to participate in the further stages of this examination and no correspondence will be entertained by the Commission in this regard.

In this period, all the candidates, who qualified for Personality Test shall also be provided an option to update the Correspondence/ Permanent Postal Address, Higher Educational Qualification, Achievement in different fields (if any), Employment Details/Service Experience, details of the Service allocated on the basis of earlier/previous Indian Economic Service/ Indian Statistical Service Examination (if any), Marital Status, PwBD Recommendation details in past, Parental details, Debarment information, earlier Examination details, OBC/EWS Annexure (wherever applicable), Socio-economic questionnaire, whichever is applicable and submit their Online Application Form.

Candidates who have uploaded the required documents/information earlier and have no information to update/fill in, are also required to mandatorily login and finally submit after verifying the details so as to generate the e-summon letter for Personality Test/Interview of IES/ISS Examination-2026. The candidates are advised to regularly visit the Commission’s website with regard to further updates.

The instruction for updating the Application Form and Rules of the Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service Examination, 2026, must be read carefully with regard to the certificates that will be produced at the time of Interview. The candidates will be solely responsible for not producing sufficient proof in support of his/her age, date of birth, educational qualification, community (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) and physical disability certificate (in the case of PwBD candidates). In case any of the written qualified candidate fails to bring any or all the required original documents in support of his/her candidature for the Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service Examination, 2026, he/she will not be allowed to present himself/herself before the PT Board and no TA will be allowed.

The schedule of the Personality Test (Interview) of candidates, who have qualified for the Personality Test, will be uploaded on the Commission’s website in due course of time. The exact date of interview will, however, be intimated to the candidates through e-Summon Letter. The candidates are requested to visit the Commission’s website (https://upsc.gov.in) for updates in this regard.

No request for change in the date and time of Personality Test intimated to the candidates will ordinarily be entertained under any circumstances.

The mark-sheet of candidates will be uploaded on the Commission's website after the publication of final result (i.e. after conducting Personality Test) and will remain available on the website for a period of 30 days.

The candidates can access the marks-sheets after keying in their Roll Numbers and date of birth. The printed/hard copies of the marks-sheet would, however, be issued by the UPSC to candidates based on specific request accompanied by a self-addressed stamped envelope. Candidates desirous of obtaining printed/hard copies of the marks sheets should make the request within 30 days of the display of the marks on the Commission's website, beyond which such requests would not be entertained.

The candidates may obtain any information/clarification regarding their issue(s) (if any) in respect of the above-mentioned Examination on Tel. No. 011-40303444/24041001 of the Commission’s Call Centre from 09:00 AM to 08:00 PM.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
President of India to present Handloom Awards 2025 on Aug 7, National Handloom Day, recognising outstanding achievement in India's Handloom Sector
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India will present the prestigious Handloom Awards during the National Handloom Day celebrations on 7 August 2026.

The function will be attended by the Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, senior dignitaries, representatives of the handloom industry, master weavers, designers, exporters, artisans, and other distinguished guests.

A total of 22 awardees, comprising 3 Sant Kabir Handloom Awardees and 19 National Handloom Awardees, will be honoured for their exceptional contribution towards preserving, promoting and advancing India's rich handloom traditions.

(List of Sant Kabir and National Handloom Awardees for 2025)

Celebrating Excellence in Handloom

The Ministry of Textiles has announced the recipients of the Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and National Handloom Awards 2025, acknowledging outstanding excellence in weaving, innovation, design development, marketing initiatives, start-up ventures and producer companies associated with the handloom sector.

The awards are instituted under the Handloom Marketing Assistance (HMA) component of the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and represent the highest national recognition for excellence in the handloom ecosystem.

The awards will be presented during the National Handloom Day celebrations to honour individuals and organisations whose work has significantly strengthened India's handloom heritage and enhanced its competitiveness in domestic and international markets.

The event is expected to witness participation from Members of Parliament, senior government officials, industry experts, academic institutions, exporters, designers and handloom weavers from across the country.

Handloom Awards

The Handloom Awards are intended to encourage excellence, innovation and sustained commitment in the handloom sector. They recognise outstanding craftsmanship, adoption of modern techniques while preserving traditional skills, product diversification, design innovation and contributions towards the socio-economic development of weaving communities.

Sant Kabir Handloom Award

 

The award is the country's highest recognition for handloom weavers who have demonstrated extraordinary craftsmanship and lifelong dedication to the preservation and promotion of India's weaving traditions.

Recipients are selected based on exceptional technical skill, innovation, sustained contribution to the sector, promotion of traditional weaving practices, mentoring of artisans and efforts towards community development.

 

The award comprises of:-

 

  • Gold Coin (Mounted)
  • Tamrapatra
  • Shawl
  • Certificate

 

National Handloom Award

 

The National Handloom Award honours handloom weavers and other stakeholders who have displayed outstanding creativity, quality, innovation and excellence in their respective fields.

The award seeks to inspire artisans and institutions to continuously raise standards in craftsmanship, product development and market outreach while preserving India's diverse handloom traditions.

 

The award comprises of :-

 

  • Tamrapatra
  • Shawl
  • Certificate

 

Selection Process

 

Awardees in the weaving category are selected through a rigorous multi-level evaluation process involving Zonal, Headquarters and Central Level Selection Committees. These committees comprise experienced professionals, technical experts and senior government officials who assess nominations against prescribed eligibility criteria and evaluation parameters.

 

For categories relating to design development, marketing, start-up ventures and producer companies, nominations undergo a structured evaluation by the Headquarters Committee and the Central Level Committee before final approval.

The selection mechanism ensures transparency, objectivity and recognition of genuine excellence across all segments of the handloom sector.

(List of Sant Kabir and National Handloom Awardees for 2025)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting to be Held in Odisha
Meeting to Deliberate on Key Priorities Including ECCE, Skill Development, Research and Innovation, Mutual Recognition of Qualifications and Academic Leadership
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Education, under India’s BRICS chairship 2026, is scheduled to host the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meeting from August 5–7, 2026 in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. These meetings would bring together education ministers, senior officials and delegates from BRICS member countries to discuss topics of collaboration, including the following priority areas:

 

(a) Strengthening Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE);

(b) Strengthening skill development and enhanced cooperation under the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance (TCA);

(c) Promoting collaborative research, innovation and start-ups;

(d) Strengthening Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ); and

(e) Capacity building for academic leadership.

 

India’s BRICS chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting the people-centric and humanity-first approach articulated by the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, at the 2025 BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro.

 

The 13th Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd Senior Officials’ Meetings would build upon a series of engagements held under the BRICS Education Track during India’s chairship. The 1st and 2nd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meetings were held earlier on 7th and 28th April 2026, respectively, followed by the BRICS Network University Conference and International Governing Board Meeting on July 20 –21, 2026. The previous engagements have helped shaped discussions and build consensus on the priority areas and proposed outcomes for the Ministerial Meeting.

 

Ahead of the 13th Education Ministers’ Meeting, the BRICS TVET Symposium and the Joint Management Committee (JMC) meeting of the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance were also held in New Delhi on August 3–4, 2026, led by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. These engagements seek to deepen cooperation among BRICS countries in technical and vocational education and training, skills development and workforce preparedness and to consolidate and exchange research and best practices across the priority themes.

 

Alongside these high-level inter-governmental engagements, India’s BRICS chairship is placing strong emphasis on youth participation and people-to-people exchanges. In this spirit, Model BRICS has been conceptualised as a student-focused initiative to be organised on the sidelines of BRICS Ministerial Meetings across India. The initiative seeks to familiarise young citizens with BRICS processes while strengthening their understanding of diplomacy, multilateral cooperation and consensus-building.

Ministry of Heavy Industries
            The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

Production Linked Incentive scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (PLI-Auto scheme) is implemented on an all-India basis. The current status of implementation of PLI-Auto scheme is as below:-

 

Parameter

Cumulative till 31.03.2026

Investment (Rs. cr)

44,326

Incremental Sales (Base Year FY2019-20) (Rs. cr)

52,414

Employment generated (Nos.)

67,820

Incentive disbursed (Rs. cr)

2,386.36

 

To boost domestic manufacturing and localisation of AAT products, PLI-Auto scheme mandates minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for availing incentives. As on 28.07.2026, 18 applicants have received DVA certificates for 155 AAT products/variants.

 

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol.

 

MHI has not conducted any study regarding incentivization of flex-fuel and electric vehicles.

 

The government has adopted a balanced approach to the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, ensuring that water sustainability, food security and farmers' interests remain paramount. Under the National Policy on Biofuels, ethanol is produced from multiple approved feedstocks, including sugarcane-based feedstocks, maize, damaged foodgrains, broken rice, foodgrains unfit for human consumption, surplus foodgrains approved by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee (NBCC) and other approved agricultural feedstocks.

The government is also promoting crop diversification towards comparatively less water-intensive feedstocks such as maize. An Expert Committee constituted by Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare in 2024 examined the water requirement of various ethanol feedstock crops & its recommendations are being considered while implementing the programme.

 

Water-use efficiency is also being enhanced through micro-irrigation, drip irrigation and other water conservation measures under the Per Drop More Crop component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana. Many sugar mills are also encouraging farmers to adopt water-efficient cultivation practices.

 

Molasses-based distilleries with incineration boilers and grain-based distilleries are required to operate as Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) units, enabling recycling and reuse of process water while eliminating liquid effluent discharge.

As on 10.07.2026, a total of 523 e-buses have been deployed across the country under the PM-eBus Sewa–PSM Scheme
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

As on 10.07.2026, the PM-eBus Sewa – Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme covers 27,555 e-buses out of the targeted 38,000 e-buses. Of these, 10,000 e-buses are under the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), 14,000 e-buses are under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), and 3,555 e-buses under various State Government/State Transport Undertaking (STU) initiatives.

 

As on 10.07.2026, a total of 523 e-buses have been deployed across the country under the PM-eBus Sewa–PSM Scheme. Further, under the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme of MoHUA covered under PSM Scheme, 400 e-buses have been allocated to the State of Odisha with no deployment as on 03.08.2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The PM E-DRIVE Scheme is being implemented on a pan-India basis, and no State-wise allocation of funds has been made. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 42,035 EVs have been sold in Assam, under this Scheme which includes 8,003 EVs sold in Cachar district. Further, a total of 40,009 EVs have been incentivised in Assam with a total reimbursement of  ₹ 99.10 crore to OEMs.

An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including the state of Assam.  Assam has not yet submitted any proposal for deployment of EVPCS under the PM E-DRIVE scheme.  

No such assessment has been done by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) for Cachar district of Assam.

The MHI is implementing following schemes to promote electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and encourage the adoption of electric public transport and commercial vehicles across the country including Cachar district and other parts of Assam:

  1. Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,297 electric buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country.
  2. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore.
  3. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries.
  4. PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore is implemented from 01.04.2024. This scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e-buses out of which 13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e-buses have been approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for deployment of EV Public Charging Stations on pan India basis. 
  5. PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme: This Scheme notified on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e-bus operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs).

 

            Following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to increase the use  of electric vehicles in the country: –

i.          GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been reduced to 5%.

ii.         The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements.

iii. MoRTH issued an advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce the initial cost of EVs.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
AGRICULTURAL ROAD MAPS BASED ON AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

As reported by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Agricultural Action Plans have been initiated for the States of Assam, Goa, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Comprehensive consultations have been undertaken with the concerned State Governments and other stakeholders for preparation of these agricultural Roadmaps.

The Agricultural Roadmap are being prepared collaboratively by ICAR, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, ICAR, ICAR Institutes, State Governments, State Agricultural Universities, and experts. The planning is based on agro-climatic regions, natural resource endowments, climate resilience, technological interventions and farmers' needs. The roadmaps aim to ensure technical validation, alignment with State priorities, local agro-climatic conditions, and climate resilience.

The Roadmap seek enhancement of productivity, profitability and resource-use efficiency in agriculture and allied sectors. The agricultural roadmaps is broad policy framework based on agro-climatic conditions. States/UTs may refer to these guiding principles while formulating annual action plans under various schemes.  The key outcomes of Agricultural Roadmap include enhancing farmers’ income, improve self-sufficiency in agricultural and allied commodities, generate rural employment opportunities and ensure sustainable growth of the agriculture sector, while addressing local agro-climatic conditions, climate resilience and farmers’ needs.

 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PREVENTION OF SOIL DEGRADATION
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has taken various measures to prevent soil degradation and promote judicious use of fertilizers, manures and herbicides by the farmers as follows-

  1. Balanced use of fertilizer is promoted under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, being implemented since 2014-15. Under the scheme, Soil Health Cards (SHCs) are generated which provide nutrient status of soil, based on which crop-wise fertilizer recommendations are provided to farmers, thereby promoting balanced and efficient nutrient management. SHC helps in enhancing crop productivity, reduce cultivation costs, and promote sustainable agriculture. So far, 26.09 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated and issued to farmers. 130627 farmer’s trainings, 7.17 lakh demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s Melas/ campaigns on soil health card recommendations have been organized across the country.
  2. National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25 November 2024.  NMNF promotes chemical-free, nature-based farming practices using on-farm inputs. Under the scheme, 23.13 lakh farmers have been registered and 11.44 lakh hectares area have been covered, Government has adopted Integrated Pest Management (IPM) as cardinal principle and main plank of plant protection in the overall Crop Production Programme since 1985. IPM is an eco-friendly approach which encompasses cultural, mechanical, biological and need based chemical control measures. The Integrated Pest Management-cum-Locust Division of Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage (DPPQ&S) promotes Integrated Pest Management (IPM) through its 48 Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs) and Locust-cum-CIPMCs located across 28 States and 2 UTs. Farmers are trained through Farmer Field Schools (FFS), 2-day HRD programmes, and safe & judicious use of pesticides awareness programmes. These programmes enable farmers to integrate cultural, mechanical and biological control measures.
  3. Special awareness Campaign and Khet Bachao Abhiyan  on balanced use of fertilizers have been conducted by Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) and ICAR during the current Kharif Season 2026 wherein total  2,94,554 programs covering 1,36,73,465 farmers have been achieved. During the campaign, farmers have also been made aware on Natural/Organic Farming, bio-inputs, alternative fertilizers etc.
  4. Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is implemented since 2015-16.  PKVY promotes organic farming by providing end-to-end support covering production, processing, certification, and marketing. So far, 18.93 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 33.63 lakh farmers have been benefited.
  5. Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) is implemented since 2015-16 to promote organic farming in North Eastern States.  So far, 2.36 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 2.74 lakh farmers have been benefited.
  6.  The Government also promotes Soil Organic Carbon Enhancer namely, Fermented Organic Manure (FOM) /Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) as a part of judicious use of fertilizers. During 2024-25, the annual consumption of FOM/LFOM was 3.36 LMT. During the current Kharif Season (1.4.2026 to 16.7.2026), the consumption of FOM/LFOM is 11.86 LMT.
  7. Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) through Directorate of Weed Research, Jabalpur is promoting sustainable Integrated Weed Management (IWM) for judicious use of herbicides in different crops and cropping systems through research, demonstrations, capacity building and extension programmes. The Directorate disseminates scientific advisories through mobile-based services, social media, printed literature and village-level extension programmes to promote the efficient and environmentally safe use of herbicides. The Directorate is also analyzing the herbicide residues in soil and food chain, and accordingly suggesting farmers for crop management practices. These interventions have significantly contributed in reducing the indiscriminate use of herbicides thereby improving soil health and crop productivity.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
RISKS AND CALAMITIES COVERED UNDER PMFBY
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), introduced in the country from 2016-17,  is voluntary for the States as well as farmers.  The scheme  provides for comprehensive risk insurance against crop damage due to non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest for the crops/areas notified by the concerned State Government.   The losses to crops due to wild animals, being preventable in nature, were therefore not covered earlier.  However, at the request of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and State Governments, States have been allowed to notify the losses by wild animals on individual assessment as add on cover at the cost of State Government.  Detailed protocol for such coverage has been provided in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme.

Inundation as a risk cover is available to all notified crops under (PMFBY).  However, for hydrophilic crops like paddy, jute, mesta, sugarcane, such cover is available except in case of localized claims.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
OILSEED AND PALM OIL PRODUCTION
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was approved on 3rd October, 2024 to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive towards self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in edible oils. The mission aims to increase primary oilseed production from 39 million tonnes (2022-23) to 69.7 million tonnes by 2030-31.

 

The NMEO-OS is implemented through a cluster-based approach. Over 600 Value Chain Cluster have been identified across the country which is managed by Value Chain Partners such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under these clusters, farmers are provided free high-quality seeds of latest high yielding varieties and training on good agricultural practices. The mission supports the establishment and upgradation of post-harvest infrastructure (oil mills) to improve oil recovery from primary and secondary sources.

 

The mission strengthens availability of certified seeds through 100% support for purchase of breeder seeds, establishment of new seed hubs and specialised seed storage units in the public sector to enhance production and storage capacity.

 

The mission focuses on improving productivity through Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs), Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLDs) and Block-Level Demonstrations (BLDs) to help farmers adopt latest varieties and good agricultural practices.

 

Oilseed production has increased from 39.67 million tonnes in 2023-24 to 43.06 million tonnes in 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW). Under the mission, 13.52 lakh hectares were covered under free seed distribution in Value Chain Clusters during 2025-26, against the annual target of 10.00 lakh hectares. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seed of recently released varieties.

 

As reported by the Directorate of Sugar & Vegetable Oils, Department of Food and Public Distribution, India imported 160.72 lakh tonnes of edible oils during 2024–25. Of this, 75.17 lakh tonnes comprised palm oil, accounting for 46.77% of the total edible oil imports.

 

The Government of India launched the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) in August 2021 to promote oil palm cultivation, with special focus on North Eastern States. The Mission is being implemented in 15 States. The mission provides comprehensive support to farmers, including assistance for high quality planting materials, inputs for intercropping and maintenance during the four year gestation period. There is also a provision for replanting of old and unproductive plantations. The mission supports farm machinery, irrigation facilities, seed gardens, nurseries and Custom Hiring Centres. The North Eastern States are provided financial assistance for setting up oil palm processing mills.

 

From 2021-22 to 2025-26, 2.73 lakh hectares was brought under oil palm cultivation, taking the cumulative area to 6.40 lakh hectares as on 31.03.2026. During this period, 114.66 lakh tonnes of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) were harvested, resulting in the production of 20.10 lakh tonnes of Crude Palm Oil (CPO). At present, 27 oil palm processing mills are operational across the country. The Mission provides Viability Gap Payment (VGP) to support oil palm growers. As on date, ₹18.90 crore has been disbursed to 9,244 oil palm farmers in Goa, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Mizoram under this provision.

 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

*****

RC/MS

(Release ID: 2294450)

item.title: MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICES (MSPs) FOR ALL CROPS
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICES (MSPs) FOR ALL CROPS Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the State Governments and Central Ministries / Departments concerned. The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICES (MSPs) FOR ALL CROPS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the State Governments and Central Ministries / Departments concerned.

The Union Budget for  2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from year 2018-19 onwards.

Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively.

In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and depots/godowns are also established at key points. The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process and during the last few years, procurement processes under MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ procurement portals ensure that the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase.

Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to reduce import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses. To encourage domestic production of  pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad and Masur under the PM-AASHA Scheme on the request of State Government from pre-registered farmers as much as offered by them through Central Nodal Agencies, namely the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF).

Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component under PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS). The objective of intervention is to protect the growers of these commodities from making distress sale in the event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices tend to fall below economic levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 percent decrease in the ruling market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request of a State/UT government.

 

Government has introduced a new component of Price Differential Payment (PDP) under Market intervention scheme (MIS) from 2024-25 season for direct payment of the price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the selling price to the farmers of perishable crops. States/UTs have an option to choose either to do physical procurement of the crop or to make the differential payment between the MIP & Sale Price to the farmers.

 

Further, from 2024-25 season, Government added another component under Market intervention scheme (MIS) for reimbursing the Storage and Transportation cost of TOP crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to central nodal agencies & State designated agencies for transporting them from the producing State to consuming states in the interest of the farmers.

 

Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data of procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The details of procurement and MSP amount paid to farmers during 2021-22 to 2025-26 (upto June, 2026) are given as under:

 

Procurement and MSP amount paid to farmers during last five years

2021-22 to 2025-26

Total Procurement (In LMT)

Total MSP Value (In lakh Crore)

5781

14.58

 

The total procurement of all 22 MSP crops has increased from 6,987 Lakh Metric Tonne (LMT) during 2004-14 to 12,819 LMT during 2014-26(upto June 2026). The MSP amount paid to farmers has increased from Rs. 7.41 Lakh Crores during 2004-14 to Rs. 27.80 Lakh crores during 2014-26 (upto June 2026).  

The Government is implementing several policies, reforms, developmental programmes to increase agricultural productivity, reduce the cost of cultivation, promote crop diversification, ensure remunerative returns and provide income support to farmers. These various schemes / programmes cover the entire spectrum of agriculture including credit, insurance,income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, seeds, mechanization,marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, extension activities,procurement of crops, digital agriculture etc.

 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
SUPPORT FOR FARMER PRODUCER ORGANISATION
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Government is implementing the Central Sector Scheme for "Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). 10,000 FPOs have been formed under the scheme since 2020-21. FPOs undertake a wide range of business activities including agri-input supply, aggregation and trading of agricultural produce, value addition and processing, seed production, digital commerce through e-market places, custom hiring services & export promotion. From the audited financial statements 2024-25 of the scheme FPOs, 6964 FPOs had a turnover of up to Rs.50 Lakh, 862 FPOs had a turnover of Rs.50 Lakh to Rs.1 Crore and 1135 FPOs had a turnover of over Rs.1 Crore. 

The National Academy of Agricultural Sciences, in Policy Paper No. 144, covers all FPOs registered in the country. The recommendations in the Policy Paper No. 144 include promotion of FPOs - industry linkages, link institutional buyers with FPOs, strengthening linkage of FPOs with Research & Development etc.    

Under the 10K FPO Scheme, financial assistance of up to ₹18 lakh per FPO is provided to meet management and handholding expenses during the initial 3 years. A matching Equity Grant of up to ₹15 lakh per FPO is  provided to strengthen the capital base of eligible FPOs and Credit Guarantee Facility for project loans of up to ₹2 crore per FPO to improve access to institutional credit.  In addition, each FPO is provided 5 years of handholding support through a Cluster-Based Business Organization (CBBO) for capacity building, business planning, market linkages, and overall institutional development.   Till date 827.81 crore has been released to the FPOs registered under the 10K FPO Scheme as management cost and Rs.631.98 crore as matching equity grant.

So far, under the 10K FPO Scheme, more than 65 lakh shareholders (predominantly small and marginal farmers) have been collectivized to leverage economies of scale.  As on date, for greater bargaining for input supply, 6928 FPOs have seed licenses, 4987 have pesticide licenses and 6650 have fertilizer licenses.  5765 FPOs have their own processing units and 3083 FPOs have availed credit guarantee.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare ICAR's Genome Breakthrough Paves Way for Better Pigeonpea Varieties ICAR-developed sequence approved as the global reference genome of pigeonpea, making it India's first fully annotated telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome High-quality genetic blueprint expected to accelerate development of climate-resilient, high-yielding and nutritious pigeonpea varieties, strengthening India's self-reliance in pulses Latest milestone builds on ICAR-NIPB's pioneering work that produced the world's first draft genome of a pulse crop in 2011 Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR's Genome Breakthrough Paves Way for Better Pigeonpea Varieties
ICAR-developed sequence approved as the global reference genome of pigeonpea, making it India's first fully annotated telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome
High-quality genetic blueprint expected to accelerate development of climate-resilient, high-yielding and nutritious pigeonpea varieties, strengthening India's self-reliance in pulses
Latest milestone builds on ICAR-NIPB's pioneering work that produced the world's first draft genome of a pulse crop in 2011
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

In a major scientific breakthrough Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed India's first fully annotated telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome of pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan L. Millsp.) variety 'Asha'. Popularly known as ‘Arhar’ or ‘Tur’, pigeonpea is one of India's most important pulse crops and a major source of dietary protein. It plays a vital role in ensuring the country's food and nutritional security.

The breakthrough builds on the pioneering work of ICAR–National Institute for Plant Biotechnology, New Delhi in pigeonpea genomics. In 2011, the institute published the world's first draft genome of a pulse crop, pigeonpea variety 'Asha', which was also the first crop genome to be sequenced entirely in India. An improved version of the draft genome was published in 2017, and the latest achievement represents its complete telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome sequence, providing the most comprehensive genetic blueprint of the crop to date.

The newly developed T2T genome sequence contains 752.65 million base pairs of DNA assembled into 92 contigs, providing a complete representation of all 11 chromosomes of pigeonpea. The genome assembly, designated NIPB_CcT2T_4, has been deposited in the global database (NCBI) under accession number GCF_000230855.1 and was released on 20 April 2026.

The genome assembly comprises all 11 chromosomes, including all 11 centromeres and 22 telomeres, demonstrating chromosome-level completeness. A comprehensive genome annotation identified 36,557 genes, producing 48,008 mRNAs (coding sequences). Transcriptome (RNA sequence) mapping recorded more than 99.9% read alignment, confirming the high accuracy and completeness of the genome.

The fully annotated T2T reference genome marks a significant milestone in India's pulse research ecosystem. It will serve as a valuable national genomic resource for advanced gene and pangenome analyses, discovery of genes associated with important agronomic and nutritional traits, and the application of molecular breeding and genome-editing technologies. The development is expected to accelerate the breeding of climate-resilient, high-yielding and nutritionally enriched pigeonpea varieties, thereby strengthening the country's pulse improvement programme. The achievement will provide a major impetus to research and innovation, benefit scientists, breeders and farmers, and contribute to enhanced productivity, improved farmer livelihoods, and India's food and nutritional security.

The ICAR plays a pivotal role by developing high-yielding, pest-resistant, and climate-resilient pulse varieties, supervising breeder seed production, conducting multi-location trials, demonstrating improved production technologies through its institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), and providing scientific support for capacity building and technology dissemination to farmers across the country.

The Government of India launched the Mission for ‘Aatmanirbharta in Pulses’ (2025-26 to 2030-31) to achieve self-sufficiency in pulse production, reduce import dependence, and enhance farmers' income through improved seeds, area expansion, technology adoption, assured procurement, and strengthened post-harvest infrastructure. The mission aims to increase pulse production to about 35 million tonnes by 2030–31 through a comprehensive strategy involving research, seed systems, and extension services.

➡️ NCBI URL link for the Reference Genome of the Pigeonpea (Arhar/Tur Dal)

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000230855.2/

➡️ REVIEW PAPER Genetic and genomic resources for accelerating marker-assisted ideotype breeding in pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan L. Millsp.)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Commonwealth Games 2026 medallists in boxing, judo and para-athletics; calls on athletes to mentor the next generation
Dr. Mandaviya highlights ₹36,000 crore expanded Khelo India scheme; says investment will ensure sustained growth of Indian sports
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, August 4: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today felicitated Indian athletes who returned from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after delivering historic performances in boxing, judo and para-athletics. 

Congratulating the champions, Dr. Mandaviya urged them to extend their contribution to Indian sport beyond their competitive careers by mentoring and inspiring the next generation of athletes.

The felicitation ceremony brought together members of the Indian boxing contingent, which topped the boxing medal tally with an impressive haul of 10 medals, including seven gold and three silver. 

The Union Sports Minister also honoured the judo contingent, which scripted India’s best-ever Commonwealth Games campaign in the discipline by securing four medals, including two historic golds, and the para-athletics contingent, whose outstanding performances in Glasgow marked a watershed moment for Indian para sport.

The medal winners were presented cash awards of Rs 30 lakh for gold, Rs 20 lakh for silver and Rs 10 lakh for bronze. 

Interacting with the athletes, Dr. Mandaviya asked the athletes to think beyond their playing careers and become contributors to the next generation of Indian sport. With the revamped Khelo India scheme now backed by a Rs 36,000-crore investment, he encouraged the athletes to consider establishing sports academies and nurturing young talent after retirement.

“Let us not just win a Commonwealth Games medal with the aim to bag a government job. I urge all of you to run sports academies once you retire from your active career,” Dr Mandaviya said, adding that the athletes’ mission should be “India first.” 

“While you were playing for the gold in Glasgow, we launched the expanded Khelo India scheme by investing a total of Rs. 36000 Crore, that will take care of greater continued investment in the growth of Indian sports in the coming years,” he added. 

Looking ahead to the Asian Games 2026, Dr. Mandaviya urged the athletes to maintain the momentum from their Commonwealth Games campaign. “I want all of you to use this morale boost to win more gold medals at the 2026 Asian Games. Those who have won silver and bronze must strive for gold, while those who have won gold must sustain this level of excellence,” the Hon’ble Minister said.

The Union Minister also urged the athletes to never forget the contribution of their coaches. “None of you should ever forget the contribution of your coaches. It is a symbol of true dedication, and the guidance of a Guru takes you a long way in life,” Dr. Mandaviya added.

India’s boxing contingent returned from Glasgow with seven gold and three silver medals, with the seven gold medals coming from Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Arundhati Choudhary (70kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg). The three silver medallists were Jadumani Singh (55kg), Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain (75kg) and Narender Berwal (90+kg). The seven gold medals also marked the best-ever performance by Indian women boxers at the Commonwealth Games.

Indian judo also received special recognition after producing its best-ever Commonwealth Games performance. 

India participated in 12 judo events in Glasgow and won four medals — two gold, one silver and one bronze, compared to three medals, with no gold, in 2022. The breakthrough was led by Khelo India athletes Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh, who created history by winning India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medals in judo. Asmita became the first Indian woman judoka to win Commonwealth Games gold, while Harsh became the first Indian male judoka to achieve the feat.

The medal-winning athletes across all sports benefited from government support through the Khelo India, TOPS and Annual Calendar for Training and Competition (ACTC) programmes, national camps at SAI NCOEs, international competition exposure, equipment and training support.


 

*****

Ayushman Kumar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Construction of Household Toilets Under SBM(G)- Phase II
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi

Sanitation is a State subject. Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)]-Phase-II is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented by the States and Union Territories (UTs) within their respective jurisdictions. As per data reported by States/UTs on SBM(G) Integrated Management Information System (IMIS), the number of Individual Household Latrines (IHHLs) constructed State/UT-wise, under SBM(G) Phase-II during last 5 years are given at Annexure-I.

Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India has been providing financial and technical support to the States/UTs to supplement their efforts to improve overall sanitation in the rural areas. In each Financial Year, funds are allocated to States/UTs based on their approved Annual Implementation Plan (AIP), past performance and budget availability. Under SBM(G) Phase-II, funds are not released component-wise/project-wise to States/UTs. States/UTs can plan for providing IHHLs, CSCs and Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) facilities under the program as per demand, local preferences, etc. as per their AIP, for their villages. The details of Central share funds allocated, released and utilized, State/UT-wise, under SBM(G)-Phase-II during the last five years are given at Annexure-III (A) to III (E).

As per the SBM(G)-Phase II Guidelines, eligible rural households are provided with an incentive up to Rs.12,000/- for the construction of one unit of Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) including for water storage facility for handwashing and cleaning to ensure hygiene. As per the programme guidelines, while selecting eligible households for providing incentive under SBM(G), the following order of preference is to be ensured by States/UTs:

I. Below Poverty Line (BPL);

II. Above Poverty Line (APL):

(i) SC/ST

(ii) Persons with disability (divyangjan friendly toilet to be ensured)

(iii) Landless labourers with homestead

(iv) Small farmers

(v) Marginal farmers

(vi) Women headed households

While ensuring the above order of preference, priority may be accorded to cover the households (against each category mentioned above) having:

  • Old Age Pensioners / Widow Pensioners / Disability Pensioners (National Social Assistance Programme {NSAP} beneficiaries) / Transgenders;
  • Pregnant and lactating mothers covered by Maternal Health Programmes of Central and State Governments, including Janani Suraksha Yojana under National Rural Health Mission; and,
  • Girl children covered by any scheme benefiting the girl child.

The identification of such households should be initiated by the Gram Panchayat in Gram Sabha meeting and to be approved by Block and District level authorities.

As per SBM(G)-Phase II guidelines, ideally the IHHL construction activities should be taken up by the individual beneficiaries themselves with support from/or through agencies in the village. The payment of incentive shall be ensured through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The progress of IHHLs construction is monitored through the data reported on SBM(G) IMIS by the States/UTs.

The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI V. SOMANNA in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha yesterday.

item.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications
item.description: Ministry of Communications TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA, during the month of June 2026, for information of general…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA, during the month of June 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 373.6 Km, Highway Drive-111.5 Km, Hotspot locations - 06, Walk Test – 4.9 Km and Inter Operator Calling at 01 location during 08th June 2026 to 12th June 2026 in J&K LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating Railway Drive, Highway Drive, City drive, Hotspots, Walk tests & Inter-operator calling, as per the legends shown on the map: -

 

Figure-1: Drive test routes

Key Parameters Assessed

    1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
    2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
    3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls.
    4. Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate.

The overall mobile network performance in Srinagar and Gulmarg City route for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 194/40350 for Airtel, 1380/40020 for BSNL, 167/37548 for RJIL and 4500/39609 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

 

  1. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/360 for Airtel, 07/340 for BSNL, 0/361 for RJIL and 3/360 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
  2. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/350 for Airtel, 39/332 for BSNL, 2/348 for RJIL and 9/344 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
  3. Data Download and Upload Throughput:

 

      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 188.64 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 10.77 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 276.92 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 24.14 Mbps for VIL (4G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

 

      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 33.69 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 6.34 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 35.90 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 10.79 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-I.

The overall mobile network performance in Anantnag and Pahalgam City route for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 226/17997 for Airtel, 3242/16735 for BSNL, 365/17914 for RJIL and 6947/15634 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

 

  1. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/161 for Airtel, 4/142 for BSNL, 0/161 for RJIL and 5/145 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  2. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 01/156 for Airtel, 17/133 for BSNL, 2/155 for RJIL and 10/111 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  3. Data Download and Upload Throughput:

 

  1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 183.84 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 6.86 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 163.53 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 12.92 Mbps for VIL (4G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

 

     ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 24.43 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 2.91 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 24.98 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 5.79 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided on the map of Annexure-II.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-II.

The overall mobile network performance in Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway Route for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

    1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 84/7890 for Airtel, 1912/7878 for BSNL, 138/7919 for RJIL and 2474/7699 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.

 

    1. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/40 for Airtel, 0/38 for BSNL, 0/41 for RJIL and 4/41 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.
    2. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/39 for Airtel, 9/35 for BSNL, 0/38 for RJIL and 1/38 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.
    3. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 192.01 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 14.61 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 88.24 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 14.27 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-III.

 

      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 34.39 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.00 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 32.05 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 5.90 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-III.

The overall mobile network performance in Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route for the    key parameters has been summarized below: -

a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 374/4876 for Airtel, 1586/4648 for BSNL, 449/4207 for RJIL and 2284/4499 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

 

b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 4/27 for Airtel, 7/26 for BSNL, 7/27 for RJIL and 7/25 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 4/25 for Airtel, 7/26 for BSNL, 0/22 for RJIL and 1/21 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

d) Data Download and Upload Throughput:

                  

                   i) Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 176.89 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.82 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 88.14 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 13.80 Mbps for VIL (4G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

 

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 36.14 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 4.20 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 33.45 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 5.09 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-IV.

 

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: -

a) City - The areas covered in the city drive are Srinagar, Rajbagh, Nowgam, Chanpora, Hyderpora, Ranbirgarh, Shadi Pora, Dab Sadat, Seh Pora, Ganderbal, Rangil, New Theed, Dani Hama, Rainawari, Soura, Hardu Aboora , Gulmarg, Anantnag, Hakura Badas Gam, Qazigund, Qaimoh, Bijbehara, Mattan, Seer Hamdan, Srigufwara, Sallar Pahalgam and nearby areas.

   b) Highway - The area covered in the Highway route are Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway passing through Pampore, Lethipora, Barsoo, Awantipora, Chersoo Awantipora,Bijbehara, Mattan,Seer Hamdan, Aishmuqam, Yanier and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway passing through Narbal, Kawoosa Khalisa, Magam, Kunzer, Cahandilora, Tungmarg and Gulmarg etc.

          c) Hotspot - The hotspot locations, capturing stationary user experience are Accounts General Office, Betaab Valley Viewpoint, Hari Singh High St., SMHS Hospital, Srinagar Railway Station and University of Kashmir Srinagar.

 

d) Walk Test - The walk test conducted on 12th June 2026, covered Lal Chowk to Ghanta Ghar capturing mobile network behaviors in crowded pedestrian environments.

 

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.ca@trai.gov or Regional Office of TRAI at Delhi RO can be contacted on telephone no. +91-11-20907772.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Cooperative based Organic Farming
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi

Organic farming is promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) in the States/UTs including Assam and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States including Assam since 2015-16 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.

Both schemes stress on end-to-end support to farmers engaged in organic farming i.e. from production to processing, certification and marketing. Primary focus of the schemes is to form organic clusters, with preference to small and marginal farmers, to create a supply chain. Both the schemes are implemented through States /UT Governments. Under PKVY, assistance of Rs. 31,500 per hectare is provided over 3 years for promotion of organic farming. Out of this, assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for on- farm /off –farm organic inputs.

Under MOVCDNER, assistance of Rs. 46,500/ha is provided over 3 years for creation of Farmers Producer Organization, support to farmers for organic inputs etc. Out of this, assistance @ Rs. 32,500/ ha is provided to farmers for off -farm /on –farm organic inputs under the scheme including Rs. 15,000 as Direct Benefit Transfer to the farmers.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi

Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops and 124 varieties in the market under the ‘Bharat Beej’ brand for distribution across the country.

BBSSL distributes its seeds through its nationwide network of member cooperative societies, private distributors and dealers, as well as through State Seed Federations and Seed Corporations under various government schemes.

For the effective implementation of its seed distribution programme, BBSSL has designated region-wise Zonal Managers and Coordinators, including officials responsible for Maharashtra and Dadra and Nagar Haveli, at its Head Office. In Maharashtra, seeds of fodder crops, cotton, sorghum and groundnut have been supplied by BBSSL through the State Government under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, namely NMEO-OS, NFSNM and the Kapas Kranti Mission, while wheat and gram seeds have been distributed through private distribution channels. In Dadra and Nagar Haveli, the Department of Agriculture has been designated as BBSSL’s Nodal Agency for coordinating seed distribution and related activities.

The BBSSL has been set up to act as an apex organization for production, procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing and distribution of quality seeds; strategic research & development; and to develop a system for preservation and promotion of indigenous natural seeds.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Financial Health of Cooperative Societies
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi

As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are 41,501 cooperative societies in Mumbai, including housing, consumer, credit and labour cooperatives. Of these, 40,853 are functional. Among the functional cooperative societies, 19,911 are profit-making and 14,877 are loss-making, while financial information is not available for 6,065 societies.

The Government approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of functional Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), including those in Maharashtra, in 2022. The objective of the project is to bring all functional PACS on a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)-based National Software. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the Project for Computerization of PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore. The project has since been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore.

Additionally, the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) provides financial assistance for infrastructure development, business diversification, value chain development, and capacity building of cooperative institutions across the country, including Maharashtra. As on 30.06.2026, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed ₹5,74,090.48 crore, including ₹3,96,763 crore during the last five years, for the development of cooperative institutions.

The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several initiatives to realize the vision of “Sahakar-se-Samriddhi” and to strengthen cooperative sector across the country including Mumbai. Key areas of initiatives include:

  1. Computerization of PACS: The Government has approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of 79,630 PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore, along with provision of IT infrastructure and implementation guidelines (Margdarshika), to promote digitalization, transparency and efficient service delivery.
  2. Model Bye-laws for PACS: Enabled PACS to undertake more than 25 business activities, improve governance, transparency and accountability in their operations. Now, PACS can operate as PM-Kisan Samridhi Kendras (PMKSKs), Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs), Common Service Centres (CSC) etc.
  3. Capacity Building and Training: Training programmes and workshops are organized for PACS officials to strengthen governance, financial management and operational capacity.
  4. Strengthening of the Three-Tier Cooperative Credit Structure: Measures have been taken to strengthen coordination among PACS, District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) to improve liquidity management and credit flow.
  5. World's Largest Decentralized Grain Storage Plan: The Government is implementing the World's Largest Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector to enhance storage capacity at the grassroots level.
  6. National Cooperative Database (NCD): The NCD has been developed to identify gaps in cooperative coverage, facilitate formation of new cooperative societies, support evidence-based policymaking, and enable performance assessment of cooperative societies through the Cooperative Ranking Framework.
  7. Tribhuvan Sahkari University: The Government has established Tribhuvan Sahkari University to strengthen cooperative education, training, research and capacity building.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

*****
