item.category: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers
item.description: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country 5 States/UTs Reduce Chemical Fertilizer Consumption Under PM-PRANAM in 2025-26 Government Expands Organic Farming, Natural Farming and Precision Nutrient Management to Improve Soil Health Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India is promoting balanced and sustainable fertilizer use through the PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment and Amelioration of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country
5 States/UTs Reduce Chemical Fertilizer Consumption Under PM-PRANAM in 2025-26
Government Expands Organic Farming, Natural Farming and Precision Nutrient Management to Improve Soil Health
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is promoting balanced and sustainable fertilizer use through the PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth (PM-PRANAM), while simultaneously expanding organic farming, natural farming and precision nutrient management to improve soil health, reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers and promote environmentally sustainable agriculture.

Approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on 28 June 2023 for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26, PM-PRANAM supports the mass movement initiated by States and Union Territories for balanced fertilizer use, adoption of alternative fertilizers, promotion of organic farming and implementation of resource conservation technologies. The scheme covers all States and Union Territories and provides incentives for reducing the consumption of chemical fertilizers, namely Urea, DAP, NPK and MOP, in comparison with the average consumption of the previous three financial years. The incentive is equivalent to 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved, of which 95% is earmarked for the concerned State/UT and 5% is retained by the Government of India. Out of the State share, 65% is to be utilized for capital expenditure projects, preferably under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, while the remaining 30% is available for other activities, including Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives.

During 2025-26, 5 States/UTs namely Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Delhi, Goa, Manipur and Mizoram recorded a cumulative reduction of 0.18 Lakh Metric Tons in the consumption of chemical fertilizers (Urea, DAP, NPKs and MOP) compared with the average consumption of the previous three financial years. The Government has informed that incentives under the scheme have not yet been disbursed.

The Government has taken several steps to train farmers in precision farming techniques for the efficient and balanced use of nutrients and to promote the large-scale production of certified organic compost through various schemes of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The details are as follows:

Organic Farming (PKVY & MOVCDNER)

Organic farming is being promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) in the States/UTs and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States since 2015-16. Both schemes stress on end-to-end support to farmers engaged in organic farming i.e. from production to processing, certification and marketing. Primary focus of the schemes is to form organic clusters, with preference to small and marginal farmers, to create a supply chain. Both the schemes are implemented through States /UT Governments. Under PKVY, assistance of Rs. 31,500 per ha is provided over 3 years for promotion of organic farming. Out of this, assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for on- farm /off –farm organic inputs. Under MOVCDNER, assistance of Rs. 46,500/ha is provided over 3 years for creation of Farmers Producer Organization, support to farmers for organic inputs etc. Out of this, assistance @ Rs. 32,500/ ha is provided to farmers for off -farm /on –farm organic inputs under the scheme including Rs. 15,000 as Direct Benefit Transfer to the farmers.

Under PKVY Scheme, since its inception (as on 30.06.2026), 18.93 lakh hectares area has been covered benefitting 33.63 lakh farmers and a total of ₹2811.36 crore (central share) has been released. Under MOVCDNER Scheme since its inception (as on 30.06.2026), 2.36 lakh hectares brought under organic farming benefitting 2.74 lakh farmers and a total of ₹1548.62 crore (central share) has been released.

National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)

The Government is also implementing the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), launched on 25 November 2024, to promote chemical-free farming integrated with livestock, diversified cropping systems and traditional Indian agricultural knowledge. The Mission has a total financial outlay of ₹2,481 crore, comprising a Central share of ₹1,584 crore and a State share of ₹897 crore, up to the 15th Finance Commission period (March 2026). Farmers adopting natural farming are eligible for an Output Based Incentive of ₹4,000 per acre per year for 2 years, limited to one acre per farmer.

`During FY 2025-26, 18,893 clusters covering 10.32 lakh hectares and involving 20.93 lakh farmers were formed under the Mission. To support field-level implementation, 33,257 Krishi Sakhis/Community Resource Persons (CRPs) have been trained and 7,601 Bio-Input Resource Centres (BRCs) established. In addition, 33.89 lakh farmers have been have been made aware about natural farming, 18.13 lakh soil samples have been collected and ₹599.68 crore has been utilized against a budget allocation of ₹725 crore during the financial year 2025-26. More than 22.47 lakh farmers have been registered under the Natural Farming Certification System (NFCS), of which over 14.43 lakh farmers have been certified.

To promote precision nutrient management, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed drip fertigation schedules for 50 crops covering 14 agro-ecological regions, which are being disseminated through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), frontline demonstrations, field demonstrations and farmer training programmes. ICAR has also standardized and promoted the use of Farm Yard Manure (FYM), phosphocompost, vermicompost, bio-enriched compost, municipal solid waste compost and enriched fermented organic manures through demonstrations, public awareness campaigns, training programmes and media outreach.

This information was provided by Smt. Anupriya Patel, Minister of State in the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Government Boosts MSME Financing Through SIDBI and ECLGS 5.0
SIDBI Expands Nationwide Presence with 71 New Branches; Direct Credit Portfolio Grows 36.8% Y-oY
ECLGS 5.0 Envisages ₹2.55 Lakh Crore Additional Credit With up to 100% Guarantee Coverage for Eligible MSMEs
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

Some major initiatives have been undertaken by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) during the last five years to improve the flow of credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across the country.

These include the following initiatives:

  1. Subsequent to Union Budget Announcement FY 2024-25, SIDBI has opened 71 new branches across India from 01.04.2024 to 29.07.2026 to expand its reach to serve major MSME clusters and provide direct credit to MSMEs.
  2. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s direct credit outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 51,687 crores, as against ₹ 37,781 crores as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 36.8%.
  3. The Bank also provides refinance assistance to augment resources of Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs) to increase their flow of credit to MSMEs. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s refinance outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 4,50,571 crore, as against ₹ 3,85,327 crore as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 16.9%.
  4. SIDBI has launched a product on co-lending arrangement with Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to provide affordable credit to smaller MSMEs, especially new borrowers, as part of its effort to reach underserved/ unserved MSMEs. During FY 202526, the Bank initiated co-lending arrangements with Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) to strengthen credit delivery and broaden financial access in underserved and untapped areas.
  5. Prayaas Scheme has been launched by SIDBI to facilitate access to affordable credit to informal micro-entrepreneurs/ micro-enterprises (IMEs), especially women and poor.
  6. SIDBI has launched a GST Sahay app for ‘on tap’ invoice-based (cash flow based) small value credit to micro enterprises using trade data and digital frameworks.

The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 in May, 2026. Under the scheme, MSMEs are eligible for additional credit up to 20% of the peak fund-based working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26.

The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) towards the amount in default for such additional credit facility extended to the eligible MSME borrowers. For the scheduled passenger airlines, the guarantee coverage is 90%.

However, the scheduled passenger airlines are eligible for additional credit up to 100% of the total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) during the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26. Under the scheme, additional credit flow of ₹ 2,55,000 crore is envisaged for MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines.  

This information was given by Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
INDIA AND UZBEKISTAN SHARE CENTURIES-OLD HISTORICAL, CULTURAL AND CIVILIZATIONAL TIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
INDIA–UZBEKISTAN PARLIAMENTARY FRIENDSHIP GROUP WILL GIVE FRESH IMPETUS TO BILATERAL RELATIONS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
H.E. MR. BAKHTIYOR SAIDOV, MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF UZBEKISTAN, CALLS ON LOK SABHA SPEAKER
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla observed today that India and Uzbekistan are bound by centuries-old historical, cultural, and civilizational ties that continue to provide a robust foundation for their enduring friendship. He expressed confidence that growing political trust, expanding trade and investment, and enhanced people-to-people exchanges will further strengthen the bilateral partnership in the years ahead. Shri Birla made these remarks during a meeting with H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan, who called on him at Parliament House. The two leaders held wide-ranging discussions on India–Uzbekistan relations, with a particular emphasis on parliamentary cooperation, trade and investment, education, culture, and issues of mutual regional and global significance.

Speaking on India's democratic traditions, Shri Birla stated that India, as the world's largest democracy, features a vibrant parliamentary system that effectively reflects the aspirations and diversity of its people. He noted that the 543-member Lok Sabha represents millions of citizens nationwide and that India's multi-party framework provides equal space for diverse perspectives and constructive debate. Referring to the functioning of the institution, Shri Birla informed the visiting dignitary that Parliament meets across three sessions annually, with the ongoing Monsoon Session actively deliberating on several matters of national importance.

Shri Birla highlighted India’s significant achievements in infrastructure development, digital innovation, technology, connectivity, investment and trade. He observed that India's youth are increasingly assuming leadership roles globally and that collaboration with leading universities and international institutions continues to expand. Referring to the India–Uzbekistan Parliamentary Friendship Group constituted in March 2026, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the initiative will impart fresh momentum to legislative engagement and deepen cooperation across economic, educational, cultural, and people-to-people spheres.

Recalling his participation in the 150th Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) held in Tashkent in April 2025, Shri Birla noted his interactions with H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, President of Uzbekistan; H.E. Ms. Tanzila Narbayeva, Chairperson of the Senate and Mr. Nuriddin Ismailov, Speaker of the Legislative Chamber. He observed that these high-level visits laid a strong cornerstone for ongoing parliamentary collaboration. Expressing satisfaction with the steady progress of bilateral relations, Shri Birla hoped that the current visit would further reinforce the comprehensive partnership between the two nations.

H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov reaffirmed Uzbekistan's firm commitment to deepening its multifaceted partnership with India, stating that Tashkent attaches high importance to expanding political, economic, and parliamentary cooperation. Appreciating India's robust democratic traditions, he noted that Uzbekistan stands to benefit significantly from the legislative experience of the world's largest democracy. Mr. Saidov further emphasized that enhanced parliamentary engagement will contribute meaningfully to advancing the comprehensive strategic partnership. He called for a shared vision to expand cooperation in trade, investment, joint projects, and emerging sectors.

To mark the occasion, H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov presented Shri Om Birla with a special commemorative publication detailing the 150th Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union hosted by Uzbekistan.

It was a pleasure to meet H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan, at Parliament House today.

We had a productive discussion on further strengthening the longstanding friendship between India and Uzbekistan, with a special focus on… pic.twitter.com/Ps18UTJdcj

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) August 4, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND EXPANSION OF NATIONAL WATERWAYS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

To encourage private investment and expand the operational network of National Waterways (NWs) for cargo and passenger traffic, the Government has notified the National Waterways (Construction of Jetties/Terminals) Regulations, 2025 to facilitate the construction and operation of terminals by private entities. Further, the Jalvahak Scheme has been launched for providing incentives up to 35% to promote cargo movement on inland waterways. The Government is also encouraging private sector participation through Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models duly assigning the O&M of terminals on long concession period.

The Jalyan & Navic portal, a One Nation One Registration single window system developed to serve as a centralized national registry for inland vessels and crew, is fully operational. Eighteen States/UTs have been onboarded on the portal and 9,953 inland vessels and 1,215 crew are registered on this portal as on 30th July, 2026.

The major challenges in increasing cargo and passenger movement on NWs include limited industrial zone along the NWs; limited availability of suitable inland vessels; inadequate first and last-mile connectivity; limited multimodal logistics infrastructure; low awareness among cargo owners and operators regarding the benefits of Inland Water Transport (IWT). To address these challenges, the Government has undertaken a number of measures which are given at Annexure.

Annexure

Measures taken to address the challenges in increasing cargo and passenger movement on National Waterways:

Development of Multi-Modal Terminals, Inter-Modal Terminals, community jetties, floating terminals and cargo aggregation hubs to strengthen multimodal connectivity and facilitate seamless cargo movement.
 

Implementation of the Jalvahak Scheme to incentivise movement of cargo through inland waterways and promote modal shift from road and rail.
 

Notification of the National Waterways (Construction of Jetties/Terminals) Regulations, 2025 to facilitate private sector investment in terminal and jetty infrastructure.
 

Development of an enabling ecosystem for deployment of inland vessels by improving fairway conditions and encouraging private participation in vessel operations.
 

Operationalization of additional routes under the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP) to improve regional connectivity and expand cargo movement.

Development of passenger and cruise infrastructure on suitable National Waterways to promote tourism and regional passenger transport.
 

Engagement with Central Ministries, State Governments, Public Sector Undertakings and private stakeholders to promote modal shift of suitable cargo to inland waterways and enhance utilization of the NWs.
 

Development of Multi Modal Logistic Parks (MMLPs) along the NWs.
 

Fairway maintenance through river training works, fairway maintenance, channel marking and hydrographic surveys.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
SHIPBUILDING PROMOTION AND MARITIME FINANCING
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has approved Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS), which is an extension of Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP), with an outlay of ₹ 24,736 crore to address cost disadvantages of Indian shipyards vis-a-vis global shipyards. The scheme guidelines to operationalize SBFAS have been issued on 26.12.2025.

Maritime Development Fund (MDF), with a corpus of ₹ 25,000 crore has been established for providing long term financing support to the shipbuilding and maritime sector. It comprises of a Maritime Investment Fund (MIF) of ₹ 20,000 crore with 49% participation from the Government of India to support equity financing for maritime sector, and an Interest Incentivization Fund (IIF) of ₹ 5,000 crore to reduce the effective cost of debt for shipyards. The guidelines for MDF have been issued on 20.02.2026. SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed as the Fund Manager for MIF on 26.05.2026.

National Shipbuilding Mission (NSbM), an inter-ministerial body, has been established as the nodal agency to oversee the implementation of Shipbuilding schemes viz. Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) and Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SBDS) launched by Government of India. Under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, proposals for the development of greenfield shipbuilding clusters in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, as well as three brownfield capacity expansion projects of various existing shipyards have been given in-principle approval, after appraisal by NSbM.

The objective of these initiatives is to position India as a global hub in the shipbuilding and maritime sector in line with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision, 2047.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
‘SEAFARER-FIRST’ INITIATIVE
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Government accords the highest priority to the safety, security and welfare of Indian seafarers, who form a significant part of the global maritime workforce. In view of the escalation of the security situation in Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and adjacent waters, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), a subordinate office under this Ministry has instituted a comprehensive and graded 'Seafarer-First' framework of measures. As part of this a real-time reporting, tracking and monitoring mechanism for vessels and seafarers operating in the said region is in place and operational. The details of steps/ measures taken by the Government are placed at Annexure.

ANNEXURE
 

Advisories to Ensure the Safety and Security of Indian Seafarers:

Following advisories operate alongside the standing maritime security architecture established under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2024 dated 10.04.2024 and are supported by a 24-hour Control Room, continuous real-time monitoring through the DG Communication Centre under DGMA, and the issue of a Situation Report every 24 hours.

DGS Circular No. 01 of 2026 dated 14.01.2026 – issued pursuant to the advisory of the Ministry of External Affairs and the Embassy of India, Tehran, advising all Recruitment and Placement Services Licence (RPSL) companies and shipping companies not to deploy Indian seafarers to Iran until further orders, and advising vessels calling at Iranian ports or transiting the Strait of Hormuz to exercise utmost caution.
 

DGS Circular No. 08 of 2026 dated 28.02.2026 – mandating comprehensive ship-shore security drills covering loitering munitions, unmanned surface vessels and similar threats, testing of the Ship Security Alert System prior to transit, voyage-specific risk assessment by owners, operators and charterers, full implementation of Ship Security Plans, and immediate reporting of any suspicious activity, interception, electronic interference or GNSS disruption to the DG Communication Centre.
 

DGS Circular No. 09 of 2026 dated 28.02.2026 – Urgent Advisory to Indian Seafarers and Shipping Stakeholders in view of Escalating Situation in Iran, requiring Indian seafarers in Iran to remain vigilant, register with the Embassy of India, coordinate for safe departure where feasible, and directing stakeholders to immediately provide details of Indian seafarers in affected areas.
 

DGS Circular No. 21 of 2026 dated 07.04.2026 - issued a safety advisory for Indian seafarers ashore in Iran and onboard vessels operating in or around Iranian waters, directing them to remain vigilant, restrict unnecessary movement, follow advisories issued by the Embassy of India in Tehran, maintain contact with company representatives, and utilize DGS emergency support channels for assistance as required.
 

DGS Circular No. 31 of 2026 dated 13.06.2026 – Precautionary Measures for Indian Seafarers in view of the Heightened Security Situation in the Gulf Region, reiterating heightened security vigilance, directing shipping companies and RPSL companies to restrict deployment of Indian seafarers to conflict areas until further orders (except emergency crew changes with consent), monitoring and reporting requirements, and dissemination of verified security information.
 

DGS Circular No. 33 of 2026 dated 26.06.2026 – issued upon improvement in the situation, superseding the earlier restriction and permitting normal operations subject to caution and applicable coastal-State security protocols, and providing for a coordinated evacuation mechanism involving the International Maritime Organization (IMO), the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), the MICA Centre and coastal States.
 

DGS Circular No. 36 of 2026 dated 15.07.2026 – issued upon renewed escalation, advising ship owners, ship managers and RPSL companies to avoid deploying Indian seafarers on vessels undertaking voyages involving passage through the Strait of Hormuz until further orders, together with heightened security vigilance and full compliance with the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.

Details of real-time reporting, tracking and monitoring mechanism for vessels and seafarers operating in the said region:

The eNavik Portal, operationalised on 01.07.2026, provides an integrated digital platform with dedicated 24x7 Marine Casualty Reporting, Crisis Management and Seafarer Grievance Redressal modules, enabling digital reporting of marine casualties, security incidents and distress situations, automated routing of incident reports to the concerned authorities, and real-time tracking of response measures and case progression.
 

An online Ship Reporting Form, has been instituted under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2024, through this all vessels transiting the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman, the Gulf of Aden, the Red Sea and adjacent waters submit their details, thereby maintaining a comprehensive and up-to-date vessel database which facilitates tracking and coordination and enables a swift response by the Indian Navy in the event of an incident.
 

A requirement, under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2026, for the Company Security Officer to furnish to the DG Communication Centre the full particulars of the vessel together with the crew list.
 

Continuous real-time monitoring is undertaken through the DG Communication Centre, which is manned round the clock, in close coordination with the Indian Navy, the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) and other competent authorities.

A Situation Report is compiled and issued every 24 hours, which records, inter alia, the vessel-wise position and the number of Indian seafarers onboard each vessel in the region.

The measures taken to ensure the safety, communication, evacuation and repatriation of Indian seafarers operating in the region are as follows:

Communication: A dedicated 24-hour Control Room and the DG Communication Centre (MMDAC) function round the clock. A defined incident-communication protocol requires contact with the nearest Indian Naval or coalition warship on VHF Channel 16 and immediate intimation to the DG Communication Centre, the IFC-IOR and the UKMTO. Since activation, the Control Room has handled 15,771 telephone calls and 36,499 e-mails from seafarers, their families and maritime stakeholders. Navigational warnings and maritime security advisories are disseminated to stakeholders on a continuing basis.
 

Evacuation and Repatriation: A total of 60 vessels have safely transited SoH carrying cargo for India. Further, 3,972 Indian seafarers have been repatriated from the Gulf region. Close and continuing contact is maintained with the families of seafarers, and dedicated welfare counsellor access has been provided wherever required. In cases of fatality, immediate financial support is facilitated, including release of Rs. 10,00,000 (Rupees Ten Lakh) through the Seafarers Welfare Fund Society.

Steps taken to ensure no Indian Seafarer is compelled to sail without adequate information, protection and support:

Regulated engagement. Every Indian seafarer is engaged through a licensed RPSL agency, and no seafarer can complete emigration clearance or sign-on formalities without formal and verified approvals. This provides an effective single point of control for the enforcement of deployment restrictions and for compliance monitoring.
 

Consent in crew changes. Where a crew change in the conflict-affected area was permitted in a genuine emergency under DGS Circular No. 31 of 2026, it was expressly made subject to the consent of the seafarer concerned. Genuine emergency cases are considered only within the applicable legal and safety framework.
 

Removal of compulsion at the systemic level. By advising against deployment on voyages through the Strait of Hormuz, the advisory removes, at the level of the system, any pressure upon an individual seafarer to accept a hazardous engagement.
 

Disclosure and due diligence. RPSL companies and seafarers are expected to verify the intended route of the vessel, its flag, the reputation and welfare record of the owner or manager, the insurance position and any exposure to conflict-affected or high-risk waters before a contract is accepted. RPSL companies are further expected to provide clear information to seafarers regarding the nature of the voyage, the trading pattern and the likely exposure to high-risk areas.
 

Grievance redressal and support. A comprehensive 24x7 grievance redressal mechanism is available through a domestic toll-free helpline (1800-889-7768), an international toll-free helpline for the United States of America (+1-888-988-0256), WhatsApp support (+91 8655856830), a dedicated e-mail address (enavik.24x7[at]gov[dot]in) and the e-Navik grievance portal, in addition to the DG Communication Centre.
 

Verified information. Stakeholders have been advised to verify incident-related information through official Government sources and to refrain from circulating unverified reports which may prejudice the interests of seafarers and their families.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
DEVELOPMENT AND MODERNISATION OF PORTS IN MAHARASHTRA
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has assessed the requirement of a deep-draft port considering the projected growth in India's cargo and container traffic, particularly on the western coast. The Deep –draft Port, officially known as Vadhavan Port, is being developed as an all-weather greenfield deep-draft major port in Palghar district. The project was approved by the Union Cabinet on 19.06.2024 at an estimated cost of ₹76,220 crore. Upon completion, the port is expected to create a total cargo handling capacity of 298 million metric tonnes per annum.

Vadhavan Port is expected to significantly improve Maharashtra's maritime infrastructure, trade competitiveness, logistics efficiency, industrial development and employment generation. The details of modernisation and connectivity projects undertaken for the development of Vadhavan port are at Annexure-I. The details of other projects undertaken for modernisation and port connectivity in the State of Maharashtra are at Annexure-II.

The efforts made by the Government towards modernisation, mechanisation, capacity augmentation and connectivity enhancement at Major Ports in Maharashtra have resulted in increase in overall capacity to 175.87 MMTPA for Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and 88.66 MMTPA for Mumbai Port Authority. In respect of non-major ports, investments have been made by the respective State Government, private port operators and the cumulative cargo handling capacity of Maharashtra's other than Major Ports has reached 130.75 MMTPA.

These initiatives are expected to strengthen India's EXIM trade, improve logistics efficiency through enhanced road and rail connectivity, promote coastal shipping, reduce dependence on foreign transshipment ports, facilitate development of port-based industries and logistics infrastructure, and generate substantial direct and indirect employment opportunities.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN UT
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has made sustained efforts to ensure the economic development of Union Territories (UTs) through a series of focused interventions, including development of world-class infrastructure, enhancement of road, sea and air connectivity, augmentation of digital connectivity, promotion of tourism, strengthening of education, healthcare, industrial development, improving urban services, bringing in governance reforms, ease of doing business, and livelihood generation, etc. The details are given at Annexure-I.

The Government has taken various measures to promote renewable and green energy in the UTs through effective implementation of schemes, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM, etc., development of utility-scale solar projects, augmentation of rooftop solar installations, promotion of household solar adoption; and other interventions.  The details of measures taken in this regard, and the benefits arising out of those are given at Annexure-II.

Annexure-I

(i) Landmark MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions) infrastructure projects like the Yasho Bhoomi Convention Centre and Bharat Mandapam in Delhi have been completed.

(ii) Strategic infrastructure projects in Jammu & Kashmir (J&K), like the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel, Z-Morh Tunnel, and the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link including the iconic Chenab Rail Bridge have been completed.

(iii) Road infrastructure has been augmented, such as the development of the Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II) and the Dwarka Expressway in Delhi, the Delhi-Dehradun and Delhi-Meerut Expressways; and construction of new motorable bridges in Ladakh, etc., which have significantly improved regional connectivity.

(iv) Construction of helipads and hangars has been completed in Ladakh to ensure connectivity to difficult terrains and for medical emergencies, even during the winter months. Air connectivity in Lakshadweep has improved with daily scheduled flights and successful trial seaplane landings. New airport terminals have been constructed at Sri Vijaya Puram in Andaman & Nicobar Islands (A&NI) and at NAMO airport, Daman.   

(v) Digital connectivity has expanded significantly in UTs, especially in island UTs of Andaman & Nicobar Islands (A&NI) and Lakshadweep. The Chennai Andaman Nicobar Islands (CANI) Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) project in the UT of A&NI and the Kochi Lakshadweep Island (KLI) Submarine OFC Project have revolutionised the digital connectivity between the islands and the mainland, enabling online education, tele-medicine,  e-governance, digital  banking  and  e-commerce.  These

initiatives have led to  reduced data costs, increased mobile and internet/broadband

penetration, and enhanced internet tele-density and speeds across the island UTs. In A&NI bandwidth has increased from 4.12 Gbps to 243 Gbps and in Lakshadweep from 1.7 Gbps to 200 Gbps.

(vi) Tourism has been identified as a key sector due to its multiplier effect on economic growth and livelihood opportunities, leading to improved standards and quality of living. The Government is actively working towards transforming UTs into global hubs of tourism. Schemes such as the Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD have been effectively leveraged to develop tourism infrastructure in UTs. Letter of award has been issued for development of 04 eco-tourism projects in A&NI. 50 tents at Bangaram and 100 tents at Thinnakara have commenced operation in Lakshadweep; and world class seafronts and premier river fronts, and tent cities have been developed in DNH&DD.

(vii) UTs have identified various niche activities, suited to their unique geography and potential, and have taken active steps to promote various kinds of traditional and experimental forms of tourism, such as winter tourism in J&K, astro tourism in Ladakh (the first-ever dark sky reserve in the country has been set up in Hanle), cruise tourism in Lakshadweep, spiritual tourism in Puducherry, eco-tourism in island UTs of A&NI and Lakshadweep, development of tourist circuits in Chandigarh, etc. All this has led to increase in tourist footfall in the UTs.

(viii) UTs have also notified their respective homestay policies to promote community-based tourism and generate local livelihoods. Moreover, local art and traditional crafts  are  also  being  promoted  in  UTs. While  5  of  the  12  Blue  Flag Certified Beaches in India are located in UTs, infrastructure facilities for blue flag certification of more beaches are being developed.

(ix) The healthcare sector has also received sufficient boost. The AIIMS, Jammu has been operationalised. Telemedicine services are now available in all inhabited islands of Lakshadweep. Healthcare facilities of NAMO Medical Education and Research Institute in Silvassa, 450-bedded NAMO Hospital in Silvassa and the 345 bedded Namo Hospital in Daman have been augmented significantly.

(x)       UTs are undertaking solar and hydro power projects to achieve power self-sufficiency with cleaner, cheaper sources of power.

(xi)      Measures have also been taken towards industrial development in UTs. To promote manufacturing and services in J&K, the New Central Sector Scheme for Industrial Development has been launched with an outlay of Rs 28,400 crore. Comprehensive investment incentives and single-window clearance mechanisms have been put in place, which has improved the investment climate in UTs. Policies pertaining to industries, land allotment, start-ups, logistics, promotion of MSMEs, etc., have been implemented by UTs, which are aimed at promoting businesses and entrepreneurship through suitable incentives, subsidies and other interventions. These measures have resulted in a big push to businesses and promoting UTs as drivers of economic growth and prosperity (AatmanNirbhar Arthavyavastha).

(xii)     Apart from the above, various measures have been taken to promote ease of doing business in UTs. Procedures for the issuance of licenses and other business-related approvals have been simplified and streamlined. Online service delivery, digital processing,  and clearances  are being  promoted  to improve efficiency and transparency, in line with the Government’s Zero Tolerance policy towards Corruption. Financial incentives have been provided under various schemes to promote entrepreneurship, MSMEs, fisheries, tourism and other livelihood activities. Digital infrastructure and e-governance is being further strengthened to facilitate service delivery. UTs have also identified certain priority economic sectors for accelerated economic growth based on their unique strengths and resources, such as developing a Blue economy, transforming into regional knowledge/IT/medical hubs, etc. 

(xiii)    As part of the broader legislative and regulatory initiatives undertaken for the UTs during the last five years, 21 measures specifically relevant to facilitating economic development were processed, comprising 19 Regulations, Bills or extensions of laws and two delegations of statutory powers. These comprise of laws related to taxation, labour regulation, stamp duty and registration, agricultural marketing, mineral development, fisheries, excise, public-service delivery and business facilitation. These measures have strengthened the enabling environment for economic development in UTs by rationalising tax and regulatory frameworks, reducing procedural delays and minor criminal compliances, ensuring time-bound delivery of business-related services, facilitating trade and property transactions, and modernising labour and sector-specific regulation. Collectively, they reduce compliance costs, improve regulatory certainty, encourage investment and enterprise, support employment generation and enable more efficient utilisation of local economic resources. Moreover, a two-pronged approach of deregulation and decriminalisation of provisions has also been adopted for promoting ease of doing business in UTs.

(xiv)    Employment generation and skill development continue to remain a priority sector for the Government. Schemes such as the PM Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), Startup India, PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana, PM Vishwakarma, PM SVANidhi, PM MUDRA Yojana, etc., are being effectively implemented in the UTs to ensure livelihood opportunities for the youth.

ANNEXURE-II

(i)        UTs are providing subsidies in addition to the central subsidy for the installation of rooftop solar plants in residential and government buildings under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. Grid-connected Rooftop Solar Plants are being promoted and installed in the UTs. Waste-to-energy initiatives have also been undertaken by UTs to promote clean and green energy.

(ii)       E-mobility is being promoted for clean and sustainable public transport in UTs. For example, electric buses have been sanctioned under various initiatives, like FAME, PM e-Drive, etc.

(iii)     UTs have notified policies regarding Electric Vehicles, renewable/solar energy, etc., such as the Renewable Energy Policy, 2024 of the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (DNH&DD), the Delhi Solar Energy Policy, 2023. Incentives have been provided within these policies and under government schemes for solar power generation. 

(iv)      Installed solar capacity has been augmented in UTs, with a special focus on solarising Government buildings. For example, Chandigarh and DNH&DD have achieved 100% rooftop solar coverage of all feasible Government residential and office buildings. UTs have also taken various other initiatives in this regard, like distribution of smokeless biomass cookstoves amongst the tribal populace in J&K.

(v)       The abovementioned energy initiatives have resulted in various benefits to the people in UTs, like, increased availability of clean and reliable electricity; reduction in electricity expenditure for households and public institutions through adoption of rooftop solar power systems; reduction in dependence on conventional fossil fuels and improvement in energy security; generation of local employment opportunities in installation, operation and maintenance of renewable energy systems, etc. All these have led to an improved quality of life through enhanced access to electricity for households, schools, healthcare institutions and community facilities, while generating direct and indirect employment.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

*****

RK/RR/PS/SC

(Release ID: 2294243)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE FOR NATURAL DISASTERS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi

As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the primary responsibility for disaster management, including disbursal of relief assistance on ground level, rests with the State Governments concerned. The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities, from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) already placed at their disposal as well as other available resources, in accordance with Government of India approved items and norms. The Central Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments and provides requisite logistics and financial support. In the case of disaster of a 'severe nature', additional financial assistance is provided from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) on the basis of the recommendations of the Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT), in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

This Ministry does not centrally maintain data regarding the loss of lives and property due to any disaster in the country.  However, the details of damages reported by State Governments/ UTs due to various hydro-meteorological disasters in the country including Himachal Pradesh during last three years i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 are as per Annexure-I.

Further, the details of State-wise allocation and releases of funds under State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) during last three years i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 are as per Annexure-II.

 

The Central Government has taken several initiatives to strengthen disaster risk reduction and enhance resilience in hilly States, including Himachal Pradesh, under the existing institutional and policy framework; as per the details provided below : -

  1. The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) and the guidelines issued by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) cover disasters such as landslides, cloudbursts, Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), forest fires and earthquakes, to which the Himalayan region is particularly vulnerable.
  2. The Government has approved the National Landslide Risk Mitigation Project (NLRMP) for implementation in 15 States, including Himachal Pradesh, with the objective of reducing mortality and economic losses by reducing the vulnerability of communities and their assets to landslides. Under the project, a Central share of ₹125.00 crore and State share of ₹14.00 crore have been approved for Himachal Pradesh.
  3. To adopt various structural and non-structural mitigation measures for addressing the risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), the National Glacial Lake Outburst Flood Risk Mitigation Programme (NGRMP) was approved for the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand.
  4. Mitigation Scheme for Forest Fire Risk Management has also been approved, under which central share of ₹ 7.34 crore and state share of ₹ 0.82 crore has been approved for Himachal Pradesh.
  5. Under the National Project for Strengthening Community Based Disaster Risk Reduction Initiatives in Panchayati Raj Institutions, a total budget of ₹14.84 crore has been allocated for Himachal Pradesh to integrate Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) practices into the Panchayati Raj governance structure through a bottom-up approach.
  6. An integrated warning system (SACHET) based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) has also been operationalized; under this system, geo-targeted early warnings are disseminated by integrating alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Geological Survey of India (GSI), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Defence Geo-informatics Research Establishment (DGRE), and Forest Survey of India (FSI).
  7. Apart from this, it is continuously strengthening multi-disaster early warning systems, disaster-resistant infrastructure, community preparedness and capacity building through initiatives like Aapda Mitra (Aapda Mitra) and Yuva Aapda Mitra Scheme (Yuva Aapda Mitra Scheme).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
MODERNISATION OF CAPF
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi

The major measures undertaken for the modernization of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) include induction of modern weapons, surveillance and communication systems, mobility platforms, force protection equipment, operational infrastructure and advanced technologies, through a Central Sector  Scheme, namely Modernization Plan-IV for CAPFs. The major items provided to CAPFs through this Scheme during the last three years include:

 

(i)      Modern weapon systems and combat equipment: Assault rifles, Glock pistols with Corner Shot systems, modern arms and ammunition and weapon accessories.

 

(ii)     Surveillance and intelligence systems: Thermal imagers, passive night vision goggles, UAVs/drones, Automatic Fire Detection and Suppression Systems and other electronic surveillance equipment.

 

(iii)    Communication and Information Technology: Secure communication equipment, Hyper-Converged Infrastructure (HCI) servers/nodes, networking infrastructure, command-and-control systems and digital operational platforms.

 

(iv)    Mobility and specialized vehicles: Medium Bullet Proof Vehicles, Light Bullet Proof Vehicles, Mine Protected Vehicles, Wheel Armoured Platforms, Emergency Rescue Fire Tenders and Rubberized Inflatable Boats.

 

(v)     Force protection equipment: Bullet-resistant jackets, ballistic helmets, protective shields and other personal protective equipment.

 

(vi)    Specialized operational equipment: Counter-IED/bomb disposal equipment, rescue and disaster response equipment and specialized tactical gear.

 

(vii)   Infrastructure: Modern training facilities, communication infrastructure, logistics support systems, ICT infrastructure, maintenance facilities and other operational infrastructure to support border guarding and internal security operations.

 

Force-wise and year-wise funds allotted to CAPFs and expenditure incurred under Modernization Plan-IV are given in Annexure-A.   

 

As a result of the modernization measures, the operational capability of CAPFs has improved significantly and these interventions have enhanced operational preparedness, mobility, situational awareness, surveillance,  force protection, intelligence gathering and response capability, thereby strengthening border guarding, counter-insurgency, anti-Naxal and other internal security operations and to effectively address emerging security challenges.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
PROVISIONS IN BNS TO DEAL CRIMES
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Government is committed to prevention and countering of the crime against women and children. In the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for the first time, the provisions relating to crime against woman and child have been given precedence and placed under one Chapter. Strict punishments up to death sentence have been provided for the offences against women. Punishment for gang rape of a woman below the age of 18 years is life imprisonment till remainder of the convict’s natural life or death. A new offence for having sexual intercourse on false promise of marriage, employment, promotion or by concealing identity, etc. has also been incorporated in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Main provisions related to protection of women and children in the new sanhitas are given in Annexure.

 

PROVISIONS FOR PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN 

 

  1. Offences against woman and child have been given precedence over all other offences in a new chapter-V of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

 

  1. In Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the age differential for minor victims of gang rape has been done away with. Earlier different punishments were prescribed for gang rape on a girl below the age of 16 years and 12 years. This provision has been modified and now gang rape on a woman below the age of eighteen years is punishable with imprisonment of life or death.

 

  1. Women have been recognized as an adult member of family who can receive summons on behalf of the person summoned. The earlier reference to ‘some adult male member’ has been replaced with ‘some adult member’.

 

  1. In order to provide more protection to the victim and enforce transparency in investigation related to an offence of rape, the statement of the victim shall be recorded through audio video means by police.

 

  1. For certain offences against woman, statement of the victim is to be recorded, as far as practicable, by a woman Magistrate and in her absence a male Magistrate in the presence of a woman to ensure sensitivity and fairness, creating a supportive environment for victims.

 

  1. Medical practitioners are mandated to send the medical report of a victim of rape to the investigating officer within 7 days.

 

  1. It is provided that no male person under the age of fifteen years or above the age of 60 years (65 years earlier) or a woman or a mentally or physically disabled person or a person with acute illness shall be required to attend at any place other than the place in which such male person or woman resides. In cases where such a person is willing to attend the police station, they may be allowed to do so.

 

  1. The new laws provide for free first-aid or medical treatment to victims of crimes against women and children at all hospitals. This provision ensures immediate access to essential medical care, prioritizing the well-being and recovery of victims during challenging times.

 

  • ix. The act of hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence, is made a punishable offence under section 95 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which entails punishment of imprisonment of minimum seven years, extendable to ten years. This provision aims to deter gangs or groups from employing/hiring children for committing offence.

 

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
ZERO TOLERANCE FOR DRUG TRAFFICKERS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi

In view of the increasing challenges of illegal narcotics trade and drug abuse, Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in coordination with concerned State and Union Territory Police, continues to undertake intelligence-led operations and preventive measures to protect youth from the menace of drugs. Various stringent actions taken under a ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy to deter drug traffickers are as under: -

(i)      To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026, which lays down a 3-year road map with clear priorities and time bound targets to be achieved by various stakeholders to control drugs with ‘Whole-of-Government’ & ‘Whole-of-Society’ approach.

(ii)     NCB, Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) and State Police are actively engaged in enforcement activity under the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. These concerted efforts have resulted in significant achievements in term of drug seizures, registration of cases, arrests, disposal of seized drugs, destruction of illicit cultivation, financial investigations and preventive detention under Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988.

(iii)    Established a 4-tier Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stake holders in the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India.

(iv)    An NCORD portal has been developed by NCB. It is an all in one portal for information related to drug law enforcement. Topics like NCORD, Training & Capacity Building, Narco-offenders data, legal information, exemplary initiatives taken by states etc are covered on the NCORD portal.

(v)     To monitor the investigation of significant and important drug cases including cases of narco-terrorism, a Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) with DG, NCB as its Chairman has been set up. So far, 11 JCC meetings at the Central level and 75 JCC meetings at the State level have been conducted.

(vi)    All Director General of Police (DGPs) of States/UTs have been requested for sensitization of beat constables, field officers and SHOs regarding Red Flag Indicators (RFI) and emerging threats relating to clandestine manufacturing of synthetic drugs, particularly Mephedrone and Amphetamine-type Stimulants (ATS).

(vii)   NCB has been regularly coordinating with other agencies like Excise, Border Security Force (BSF), State ANTF etc. to conduct joint operations to control the drug trafficking.

(viii)  Financial investigations and effective implementation of the PITNDPS is being regularly emphasized at forums viz. NCORD, JCC, Regional Conference for dismantling and weakening of organized synthetic drug trafficking networks. 

(ix)    Comprehensive guideline on financial investigation, facilitating systematic identification, tracing and attachment of proceeds of crime have been issued.

(x)     For the capacity building of Drug Law Enforcement Officers and Agencies, NCB organizes workshops/ seminars/ training programmes. NCB is regularly conducting specialised training programmes on investigation of clandestine laboratories and precursor chemical diversion in collaboration with the United States-Drug Enforcement Administration (US-DEA), with participation of officers from Central Agencies and State DLEAs.

(xi)    India holds regular Director General (DG) Level/Bilateral talks on drug related matters with countries such as Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Singapore, United States of America (USA).

(xii)   NCB has strengthened international cooperation in drug control through bilateral agreements with 27 countries and Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with 19 countries.

 

(xiii)  A National Narcotics Helpline "मादक-पदार्थ निषेध आसूचना केंद्र" (MANAS) was launched as a 24x7, toll-free National Narcotics Call Centre. MANAS has been envisioned as an integrated system providing a single platform for citizens to log, register and resolve drug related issues/problems through various mode of communications like call (1933), e-mail, web portal & UMANG mobile app. 

(xiv)  Launched "Mission Drug Free Campus" in various educational institutions, universities all over India, in which special focus is being given to the youth and they are being sensitized about the importance of drug free campuses.

 

As domain specific initiatives, Government through NCB has adopted an intelligence-led and technology driven approach to identify and dismantle drug trafficking networks operating through online platforms, encrypted communication applications and the Darknet. The steps taken in this regard are as under:

    1. Strengthened capabilities to counter technology enabled drug trafficking by engaging cyber experts to investigate darknet enabled drug trafficking and cryptocurrency-based transactions.
    2. To enhance the technical expertise of enforcement personnel, NCB, in  collaboration  with  the  US-DEA  and Rashtriya  Raksha  University

(RRU), Gandhinagar, has conducted several capacity building programmes for officers of NCB and other Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) on cyber enabled narcotics investigations, digital forensics, darknet monitoring, cryptocurrency investigations and other emerging technologies used in drug trafficking.

 

Furthermore, the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029) has been released on 26.06.2026 envisages the establishment of dedicated Darknet and Cryptocurrency Cells in all Anti-Narcotics Task Forces (ANTFs), adoption of advanced technologies and AI-enabled analytics, research, capacity building of agencies and enhanced inter-agency coordination to dismantle organized cyber enabled drug trafficking networks.

The administration of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 lies with the Department of Revenue. The Government undertakes periodic reviews of the provisions of the NDPS Act, taking into account judicial pronouncements, implementation experience, and gaps identified by enforcement agencies and stakeholders. Based on such reviews and keeping in view emerging challenges, amendments to the Act are proposed wherever considered necessary. This forms part of the Government’s continuous legislative review process to ensure that the statutory framework remains effective, contemporary and responsive to evolving requirements.

The Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) inter-alia has focused on creating Drug Free Campus (+500 meter) around educational institutions. Further, consent-based screening Test for students as part of student wellness programme is also proposed in the Vision Document at Centrally Funded Higher Educational Institutions. The initiative forms part of the three-year, time bound roadmap under the Vision Document, which also promotes Drug Free Campuses, preventive education, awareness programmes, counselling and community participation to create a safe and drug-free environment in educational institutions.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

   * A Sender is a Principal Entity or Telemarketer who owns one or more telephone numbers or the SMS headers used for communication.

 

Key Insights:

❖ Overall, action was taken against 183 thousand telecom resources along with blacklisting of 263 senders in Q1 / FY 2026-27.

❖ Enforcement targeted multiple layers – outgoing barring, long-term disconnection, sender blacklisting across all operators and SMS header blocking – to curb repeat violations.

❖ Against 730.82 billion total calls originated in the telecom network in the country in Q1 of FY 2026-27, total UCC complaints stood at 1.085 million i.e. approximately 1.5 complaints per million calls.

TRAI DND App

Consumer participation through the TRAI DND App continued to play a critical role in strengthening enforcement against spam communications. The App is a tool for consumers to register and modify their preferences for blocking or receiving promotional communications with ease.  

Item

Key Statistics (rounded off)

Total App Downloads as on 30.06.26

3.316 million

89%

Key Insights:

❖ The TRAI DND App accounts for 89% of all UCC complaints received by the Access Providers.

DND Preference Registrations

Consumers can use the TRAI DND App, their telecom service provider’s App/ Website, or call/ send SMS to 1909 to register and modify their Do Not Disturb (DND) preferences for blocking or receiving promotional communications from the senders from any or all the sectors.

Parameter

Key Statistics (rounded off))

Total Preferences Registered at DND Registry as on 30.06.2026.

224 million

Total Subscriber Base in the country as on 30.06.2026

1.348 billion

Pecentage of Registered Preferences.

16%

Key Insights:

❖ More than 1.12 billion subscribers have not registered any preference, and, hence, are accessible for all commercial communications from registered telemarketers and senders. The consumers desirous of controlling commercial communications can register their preferences on DND registry.

TRAI Designated Series: 140xx and 1600xx

TRAI introduced the designated 140 series for promotional calls to ensure that such calls originate from a dedicated numbering series, enabling consumers to easily identify and manage such calls. The calls originating from 140 series numbers are pre-verified against the preferences of the customers before delivery. The designated series enables the consumer to exercise the choice of accepting or declining the call.

The 1600 series was introduced for service and transactional calls by the entities in Banking, Financial services & Insurance sector, and for Government to citizen communication. This designated series  provides trusted calling numbers for such important communications.

Together, these dedicated numbering series improve transparency, consumer trust, and the effectiveness of regulatory enforcement against spam and fraudulent communications.

Key Insights:

❖ Registered DND preferences enabled blocking of about 1.48 billion promotional calls and 7.30 billion promotional SMSs, demonstrating effective consumer preference enforcement.

❖ 13.16 billion promotional calls and 248.06 billion commercial SMS were routed through registered communication channels.

AI-Based Suspected Spam Flagging on Incoming Calls

In order to alert the consumers from suspected spam calls and SMS from entities using normal 10-digit numbers that bypass the regulated system, AI-based systems have been deployed by the Telecom Service providers (TSPs) to flag such suspected spam on the basis of calling pattern analysis. Further, the telecom service providers have started sending warning notifications to entities suspected with high probability of sending such spam. An entity could be using multiple numbers for sending spam. These notifications warn the suspected senders of regulatory action so as to refrain from sending further spam.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Government Develops Industrial Townships Under NICDP Through Centre-State Partnership Model
Government Approves 20 Industrial Nodes Under NICDP; ₹16,172.95 Crore Sanctioned for Industrial Corridor Development
Four Industrial Corridor Projects Completed with World-Class Infrastructure; Government Fast-Tracks Remaining Nodes
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi

Government of India has undertaken development of industrial townships under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP), through Special Purpose Vehicles formed jointly with the State Government. The project development activities include identification of industrial nodes as per the prioritisation of the State government, followed by preparation and approval of concept master plan and development plan, environmental clearance and detailed design plan by the State government, prior to consideration of the project for approval. The State Government contribution is in the form of land and Govt of India’s contribution is in the form of equity and/or debt.

Government of India has approved a total of 20 industrial nodes under NICDP. Out of these, 12 projects were approved during the last 5 years. The State wise details of these projects is at Annexure I.

Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has sanctioned and released funds amounting to Rs.16,172.95 Crore to National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) for development of Industrial Corridor Projects. NICDIT has further released funds to the extent of Rs.14,569.97 Crore to the project SPVs to carry out project development for various industrial nodes/projects under NICDP.

Details regarding the funds released to the project SPVs by NICDIT for the approved projects, State and project-wise is at Annexure II.

Out of the 20 projects approved under NICDP, four projects have been completed. The current status of ongoing projects (16 no.) under NICDP is at Annexure III. The total construction timeline for project completion is 36-48 months from the actual date of appointment of EPC contractor.

The internal trunk infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and power distribution within the industrial city/node, are executed through EPC contractors engaged by the respective project SPVs. External connectivity infrastructure such as bulk water supply, power, telecom and roads—have been comprehensively mapped and examined on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP) portal and undertaken by concerned state SPVs as per SHA/SSA conditions in consultation with State department/Central agencies.

The following steps are taken to expedite implementation and ensure timely

completion of projects:

 

  • An Apex Monitoring Authority periodically reviews the activities of NICDIT and the progress of the Industrial Corridor projects
  • DPIIT through NICDIT periodically monitors the development of these projects with the officials of State Govt(s)/respective agencies/stakeholders.
  • All necessary regulatory as well as statutory clearances are obtained on time through coordination with stakeholders and line agencies to reduce risk.
  • Regular monitoring at various levels is carried out and necessary policy interventions are made wherever required.
  • The PRAGATI and PMG portals are leveraged to fast-track project implementation and ensure timely completion to remove bottlenecks wherever required.

item.description: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh reviews reforms in Central Administrative Tribunal; says technology-driven governance is strengthening administrative justice CAT Chairman Justice Ranjit Vasantrao More informs the Minister that the Tribunal is maintaining an overall disposal rate of more than 93 per cent Digital transformation and improved case disposal mark new phase of reforms in CAT: Dr. Jitendra Singh Government committed to making administrative justice faster, transparent and technology-driven: Dr. Jitendra Singh Posted…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh reviews reforms in Central Administrative Tribunal; says technology-driven governance is strengthening administrative justice
CAT Chairman Justice Ranjit Vasantrao More informs the Minister that the Tribunal is maintaining an overall disposal rate of more than 93 per cent
Digital transformation and improved case disposal mark new phase of reforms in CAT: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Government committed to making administrative justice faster, transparent and technology-driven: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi

Chairman of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Justice Ranjit Vasantrao More, called on Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, and Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, and briefed him on the Tribunal's recent initiatives aimed at strengthening administrative justice through institutional reforms, wider outreach and technology-enabled service delivery.

Justice More informed the Minister that since its inception the Tribunal has received more than 10 lakh cases for adjudication and disposed of over 9.32 lakh cases, maintaining an overall disposal rate of more than 93 per cent.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has consistently pursued governance reforms that make public institutions more transparent, efficient and citizen-centric. He said administrative justice is an integral component of good governance and reforms must continuously improve accessibility, efficiency and ease of service delivery for government employees across the country.

The Minister said the transformation taking place across public institutions is being driven by a strong emphasis on technology, transparency and process simplification. He said digital platforms are helping institutions deliver services faster, improve accountability and reduce procedural delays, thereby making governance more responsive to the needs of citizens.

Referring to the progress made by the Central Administrative Tribunal, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Tribunal's expanding digital ecosystem, strengthening infrastructure and sustained improvement in case disposal reflect the broader direction of governance reforms being pursued by the Government. He said these initiatives are contributing towards a more efficient and accessible administrative justice delivery system.

The Minister said expanding access to justice remains an important priority. He said the establishment of new Benches and commencement of Circuit Sittings in geographically distant regions have brought administrative justice closer to litigants, reducing travel and improving convenience for government employees serving in different parts of the country.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said institutional reforms are most meaningful when they produce measurable outcomes. He said continued improvement in disposal of cases alongside modernisation of judicial processes demonstrates the value of sustained reforms backed by technology and better administrative systems.

Justice Ranjit Vasantrao More apprised the Minister that the Tribunal has undertaken several important initiatives during the past few years, including establishment of new Benches at Jammu and Srinagar and commencement of Circuit Sittings at Puducherry, Leh, Kargil and Vijayawada, thereby expanding access to administrative justice in remote and underserved regions.

The Chairman also briefed the Minister on the significant progress achieved under the Advanced Case Information System (ACIS), which has enabled a wide range of digital services including e-filing, virtual hearings, online display boards, SMS and e-mail alerts, online payment of court fees, mobile application, e-certified copies, digital inspection of judicial records, advanced search facilities, e-mentioning, e-listing and paperless court functioning through a document management system.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said such initiatives are fully aligned with the Government's vision of Digital India, where technology serves as an enabler of transparency, efficiency and ease of governance. He said digital transformation is creating institutions that are more accessible, responsive and future-ready.

During the meeting, Justice More informed the Minister that since its inception the Tribunal has received more than 10 lakh cases for adjudication and disposed of over 9.32 lakh cases, maintaining an overall disposal rate of more than 93 per cent. He also apprised the Minister that pendency has declined significantly in recent years despite continued inflow of fresh cases, while annual disposal during 2025 exceeded fresh institutions.

The Chairman further briefed the Minister on the implementation of e-Office across all Benches, onboarding of officers and staff on e-HRMS, adoption of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS), digital processing of pension cases through the Bhavishya Portal and implementation of e-SAM as part of the Tribunal's broader digital governance initiatives.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government will continue to support reforms that strengthen institutional capacity, improve public service delivery and leverage technology to build efficient, accountable and citizen-centric institutions. He said the objective is to ensure that governance reforms continue to translate into tangible benefits for employees and citizens alike.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Ayurveda Day and Promotion of Preventive Healthcare
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi

The 10th Ayurveda Day was celebrated on 23rd September 2025 under the aegis of the Ministry of Ayush, with All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), Goa as the nodal institute. The celebrations were held on the theme “Ayurveda for People and Planet,” emphasizing holistic health and environmental sustainability.

The main event at AIIA, Goa was held in the august presence of Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju, Hon’ble Governor of Goa (Chief Guest), and was graced by Dr. Pramod Sawant, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Goa; Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Hon’ble Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush & Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare; and Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy. The prestigious National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards were conferred upon eminent Vaidyas in recognition of their outstanding contributions to the field of Ayurveda. Multiple projects/initiatives were also inaugurated/launched during the event.   The details of major projects/initiatives are given at Annexure I.

Beyond the main event at AIIA Goa, extensive activities were organised across the country and abroad as a part of Ayurveda Day 2025 including Ayurveda health camps providing free consultations, diagnostic services, and distribution of medicines; specialized camps focusing on non-communicable diseases, geriatric care, women and child health, and lifestyle disorders; and outreach services in rural and underserved areas to improve accessibility to traditional healthcare. Educational and awareness initiatives formed a major component, with the organization of seminars, national and international conferences, CME programmes, workshops, and expert lectures. Schools, colleges, and community institutions actively participated through quizzes, essay competitions, painting competitions, and awareness drives to sensitize the younger population about healthy lifestyles rooted in Ayurveda. In alignment with the theme “Ayurveda for People and Planet,” numerous activities focusing on environmental sustainability were also conducted, including plantation drives, herbal garden development, medicinal plant distribution, and cleanliness campaigns under Swachhta initiatives. Digital outreach played a significant role, with webinars, social media campaigns, online pledge drives, and interactive programmes conducted through platforms such as MyGov, significantly amplifying public engagement and awareness.  The Day was observed across more than 150 countries.

A total of 32 States and Union Territories reported organization of activities in connection with Ayurveda Day 2025. The major activities included Ayurveda medical camps, medical screening and outreach programmes, awareness campaigns, seminars, workshops, webinars, Yoga sessions, medicinal plant exhibitions, plantation drives, distribution of medicinal plants, cleanliness drives, rallies, walkathons, competitions, media and Information Education and Communication (IEC) activities. The list of States and Union Territories that reported Ayurveda Day 2025 activities is placed at Annexure II.

To further institutionalise Ayurveda Day as a nationwide movement for preventive healthcare, and public awareness, the Government has notified 23rd September as the annual date for its observance, thereby providing a fixed date for its celebration every year. The Ministry of Ayush adopts a Whole-of-Government approach by involving Central Ministries/Departments, States/UTs, National Institutes, Research Councils, academic institutions and other stakeholders. A dedicated theme is identified each year, and a framework of suggested activities aligned with the theme is circulated to stakeholders to facilitate coordinated nationwide implementation, with a consistent focus on preventive healthcare, health promotion, and public awareness through Ayurveda. A nodal institution under the Ministry is designated annually for overall coordination for planning, implementation, and monitoring of activities. A dedicated Ayurveda Day microsite serves as a central repository of the IEC materials, and other resources, besides enabling online reporting and documentation of activities. These measures facilitate coordinated nationwide outreach, promote preventive healthcare, and enhance public awareness of Ayurveda.

 

 

Annexure I

Details of projects/initiatives inaugurated/launched during the main event of 10th Ayurveda Day held at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa

 

1.         Inauguration of facilities

  1. Integrative Oncology Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa
  2. Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD) - Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa
  3. Blood Storage Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa
  4. Hospital Linen Processing & Care Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa

2.         Launches

  1. Guidelines for Examining Ayush Related Interventions by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks (CGPDTM)
  2. Launch of nationwide campaign - “Desh ka Swasthya Parikshan” - for the assessment of the health status of individuals
  3. Launch of the website - ‘Admirable Personalities to Transform Ayurveda (APTA)’- prepared by CCRAS as a tribute to the luminaries in the field of Ayurveda.
  4. Launch of web- based portal – ‘Digitized Retrieval Application for Versatile Yardstick of Ayush Substances (DRAVYA)’ - developed by CCRAS
