item.title: Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Over 1.20 Crore People Sensitised in Jammu & Kashmir; 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras Join the Campaign Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government is implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) to prevent substance abuse through sustained awareness campaigns, de-addiction, rehabilitation and counselling services across the country. In the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir, the campaign…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
Over 1.20 Crore People Sensitised in Jammu & Kashmir; 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras Join the Campaign
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) to prevent substance abuse through sustained awareness campaigns, de-addiction, rehabilitation and counselling services across the country. In the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir, the campaign has reached more than 1.20 crore people, including over 69.14 lakh youth and 51.20 lakh women, while 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras have joined the nationwide movement against drug abuse, as on July 29 this year. The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the campaign under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma shared the details in a written reply to Shri Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi in Lok Sabha. The House was informed that the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, NGOs and Government Hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and capacity-building programmes to reduce drug demand across the country.

The written reply further stated that the Ministry is supporting a comprehensive network of de-addiction and rehabilitation facilities in Jammu & Kashmir, including Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), 3 Outreach and Drop-In Centres (ODICs), 2 Community-Based Peer-Led Intervention (CPLI) programmes, 6 District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs), and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) established in Government hospitals across the Union Territory.

The House was also informed that the Ministry operates the National Toll-Free De-addiction Helpline 14446, which provides primary counselling and referral services. The helpline has received more than 4.6 lakh calls across the country, including over 11,000 calls from Jammu & Kashmir, reflecting increased awareness and accessibility of support services.

The reply further highlighted that the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, launched on 15 August 2020, has now been expanded to all districts of the country. The campaign focuses on educational institutions, universities and schools to create awareness against substance abuse through community participation. Nationally, the campaign has sensitised more than 29.05 crore people, including over 11.05 crore youth and 7.81 crore women, while more than 1.17 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras have joined the movement.

Replying to the query regarding assessment of the campaign, the House was informed that the implementation of NMBA is regularly reviewed through monthly review meetings, Chintan Shivirs and National-Level Conferences with States and Union Territories. States and UTs are encouraged to establish and regularly convene State, District and Block-level NMBA Committees to strengthen coordination and ensure effective implementation. These efforts have contributed to sustained awareness generation, increased community participation, stronger inter-departmental coordination, and improved outreach for prevention, treatment and rehabilitation services for persons affected by substance abuse.

Ltd. to Expand Tourism and Employment Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi The hospitality and tourism sector plays a vital role in driving economic growth, creating employment opportunities and promoting regional development. However, expanding businesses in this sector often requires substantial financial support to develop world-class infrastructure and meet growing customer expectations. Demonstrating how institutional support…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Creating a Premier Hospitality and Recreation Destination: How VCF-SC Enabled BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. to Expand Tourism and Employment
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

The hospitality and tourism sector plays a vital role in driving economic growth, creating employment opportunities and promoting regional development. However, expanding businesses in this sector often requires substantial financial support to develop world-class infrastructure and meet growing customer expectations. Demonstrating how institutional support can accelerate entrepreneurial growth, BP Sons Pvt. Ltd., established in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, owned by Manish Verma, has emerged as a leading destination for recreation, hospitality and social events. The company's journey reflects the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. has established a modern amusement park featuring electrical and mechanical rides, water-based recreational activities, multi-cuisine dining facilities and a well-equipped banquet hall for weddings, conferences and social gatherings. With its quality infrastructure and integrated hospitality services, the enterprise has gained strong recognition and built a loyal clientele across the region.

Mr. Manish Verma

Recognising the project's potential to generate employment and contribute to the local economy, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹4.81 crore in 2015 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The financial support strengthened the company's expansion plans and enhanced its operational capabilities.

Integrated Amusement Park, Banquet Hall & Hospitality Services

The financial assistance enabled the company to expand its existing business operations, strengthen community engagement, enhance premium wedding and event services under a unified business model and meet the increasing demand for quality hospitality services. The project also generated direct and indirect employment opportunities for local people while helping the enterprise establish a strong customer base in the competitive hospitality sector.

Amusement Park Facility

Integrated Amusement Park, Banquet Hall & Hospitality Services

The impact of the intervention has been significant. Today, the enterprise has increased its total workforce from 14 to 25 employees, including 12 Scheduled Caste/Backward Class employees and 13 non-SC/BC employees. The company's asset base has also witnessed remarkable growth, increasing from ₹1.21 crore to ₹6.65 crore, reflecting sustained business expansion and improved financial strength.

Mr. Manish Verma

Reflecting on the journey, Mr. Verma said:

"The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, enabled us to expand our business, strengthen operational stability and enhance our hospitality and event services. Today, BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. has established a strong customer base and continues to generate employment while contributing to the growth of the hospitality sector in Uttar Pradesh."

The success of BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial support under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) is enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish sustainable enterprises that generate employment, strengthen regional tourism and hospitality infrastructure and contribute to inclusive economic development. By fostering entrepreneurship and supporting business expansion, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower entrepreneurs, create livelihoods and build sustainable futures across the country.

SS-08-TAR-KV-GA
Date – August 03, 2026

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Odisha has been a land with a rich tradition of knowledge, culture, spirituality and service. For…
item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA INAUGURATES JAGADGURU KRIPALU UNIVERSITY AT CUTTACK
OUR UNIVERSITIES MUST CREATE AN ENVIRONMENT WHERE YOUNG PEOPLE CAN DEVELOP THEIR TALENTS AND REALIZE THEIR DREAMS AND ASPIRATIONS: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the Jagadguru Kripalu University at Cuttack, Odisha today (August 3, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Odisha has been a land with a rich tradition of knowledge, culture, spirituality and service. For centuries, this sacred land of Mahaprabhu Jagannath has spread the message of inclusivity, compassion and human welfare. The region of Cuttack is the birthplace of great luminaries such as 'Utkal Gourav' Madhusudan Das, 'Karmavir' Gauri Shankar Ray, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, and Biju Patnaik. It is also the workplace for 'Utkalmani' Pandit Gopabandhu Das and 'Utkal Kesari' Dr. Harekrushna Mahtab. Cuttack’s contribution to the fields of public service, literature, and culture has been immensely significant and inspiring. It is expected that the Jagadguru Kripalu University, established in such a glorious region, will serve as a powerful medium for the service of society and the nation by integrating India's ancient cultural and spiritual traditions with modern education.

The President said that India is among the countries with the youngest populations in the world. This is our greatest asset. To make optimal use of this asset, our universities must create an environment where young people can develop their talents and realize their dreams and aspirations. They must be provided with value-based education. Universities bear the responsibility of shaping citizens guided by integrity, discipline, sensitivity and a commitment to the national interest. She stated that the knowledge acquired by the youth becomes truly meaningful only when it is used in the service of humanity, the welfare of society, and the progress of the nation.
 

The President said that we have set a goal to build Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. Our higher education institutions play a pivotal role in achieving this objective. She urged universities to function as centres of knowledge where the ideas and technologies developed address the needs of society. She said that while embracing modern knowledge, students should remain committed to ethical values. She was happy to note that Jagadguru Kripalu University will foster research, innovation, and entrepreneurship while emphasizing the cultural and spiritual growth of students. She expressed confidence that this university will produce skilled manpower, researchers, and entrepreneurs who will contribute to realizing the goals of a ‘Viksit Odisha’ and a ‘Viksit Bharat’.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Driving Clean Energy and Sustainable Entrepreneurship: How VCF-SC Enabled Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. to Establish a Successful Solar Power Project
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

India's transition towards clean and renewable energy requires innovative entrepreneurs backed by timely financial support. Recognising the importance of promoting sustainable enterprises while creating employment opportunities, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been supporting Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs in establishing commercially viable businesses. One such success story is Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd., owned by Dasari Kumari, located in Nalgonda, Telangana, which has successfully established and operates a 1 MW Solar Power Plant, contributing to clean energy generation and regional economic development.

Recognising the project's potential, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹4.35 crore in 2016 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The financial support enabled the company to establish the solar power project and strengthen its long-term operational and financial sustainability.

Ms. Dasari Kumari

The financial assistance enabled Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. to successfully commission and operate a 1 MW Solar Power Plant, generating clean and sustainable energy while improving operational efficiency. The enterprise has consistently achieved its expected performance targets and generates stable revenue in line with planned financial projections. The project has also strengthened environmental sustainability by promoting renewable energy generation in the region.

Solar Power Plant

Sustainable Growth Through Renewable Energy

The intervention has created a significant socio-economic impact. The enterprise is operating successfully with improved financial growth and has generated both direct and indirect employment opportunities for local people. It has also established strong market linkages with clients, ensuring sustained business expansion and long-term commercial viability while contributing to India's clean energy mission.

Reflecting on the journey, Ms. Dasari Kumari said:

"The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, enabled us to establish our solar power project successfully. The assistance strengthened our business operations, improved financial sustainability and helped us generate clean energy while creating employment opportunities for the local community."

 

The success of Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial support under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) is empowering Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish sustainable enterprises in emerging sectors such as renewable energy. By supporting entrepreneurship, generating employment and promoting environmentally sustainable development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to build inclusive growth and sustainable futures across the country.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Expanding Access to Affordable Healthcare: How VCF-SC Enabled Aboli Hospital to Build a Modern Multi-Speciality Healthcare Facility
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Anil Sadashivrao Kamble

Quality healthcare is a cornerstone of inclusive development. However, access to advanced medical facilities remains a challenge for people living in semi-urban and rural regions. Demonstrating how entrepreneurship coupled with institutional support can bridge this gap, Aboli Hospital Private Limited, established by Dr. Anil Sadashivrao Kamble in Parbhani, Maharashtra, has emerged as a trusted multi-speciality healthcare institution. The hospital's journey reflects the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Aboli Hospital Private Limited has established a 70-bedded multi-speciality hospital equipped with a pharmacy, advanced Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and critical care facilities capable of treating complex medical emergencies, particularly paralysis and other critical illnesses. The hospital provides quality and affordable healthcare services under one roof for the people of Parbhani and neighbouring districts. Recognising the project's social and healthcare impact, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹5 crore in 2023 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The support also enabled the hospital to procure modern medical equipment, reduce the burden of high-cost bank loans and strengthen linkages with health insurance schemes, including Ayushman Bharat.

Facility

Multi-Speciality Hospital & Advanced Critical Care Facility

The financial assistance enabled the hospital to establish modern healthcare infrastructure, strengthen advanced ICU and critical care services, procure state-of-the-art medical equipment and expand access to affordable healthcare for underserved communities. The institution has also developed strong linkages with government healthcare schemes, insurance providers and specialised medical practitioners, enhancing the quality and reach of healthcare services across the region.

Multi-Speciality Hospital & Advanced Critical Care Facility

The impact of the intervention has been significant. Today, the hospital has generated 65 direct employment opportunities, including 27 Scheduled Caste employees and 38 non-Scheduled Caste employees. The enterprise has witnessed remarkable financial growth, with its net worth increasing from ₹61.75 lakh to ₹6.93 crore, while creating assets worth ₹2.78 crore. The project has emerged as a model of inclusive healthcare entrepreneurship by providing affordable, quality medical services while creating sustainable livelihoods and strengthening healthcare delivery in the region.

Dr. Anil Sadashivrao Kamble, Managing Director

Reflecting on the journey, Dr. Kamble said:

"The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, strengthened our mission of delivering quality and affordable healthcare services to underserved communities. Today, Aboli Hospital stands as a trusted critical care and multi-speciality healthcare institution, improving access to advanced medical treatment across the region."

Multi-Speciality Hospital & Advanced Critical Care Facility

The success of Aboli Hospital Private Limited demonstrates how targeted financial support under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes is enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish socially impactful enterprises that strengthen healthcare infrastructure, generate sustainable employment and improve access to quality medical services. By fostering entrepreneurship and promoting inclusive development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower entrepreneurs, create livelihoods and ensure that essential healthcare reaches underserved communities across the country.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
47,328 Villages Selected Under PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component Across the Country; 435 Villages in Telangana
Over 3.28 Lakh Development Works Identified and More Than 47.59 Lakh Beneficiaries Saturated Under the Scheme
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) to promote the socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities through the integrated development of villages under its Adarsh Gram Component. The scheme aims to ensure saturation of key socio-economic indicators through convergence of Central and State Government schemes while addressing critical development gaps.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Shri Anil Kumar Yadav Mandadi in the Rajya Sabha, informed that 47,328 villages have been selected across the country under the Adarsh Gram Component of PM-AJAY, including 435 villages in Telangana. State-wise details of the selected villages have been placed on the Table of the House.

The Minister further informed that the Adarsh Gram Component focuses on the integrated development of selected villages through the saturation of 50 monitorable socio-economic indicators across 10 development sectors, including education. A Need Assessment Survey is conducted to establish the baseline status of these indicators. The identified gaps are addressed through convergence with Central and State Government schemes or through interventions supported under PM-AJAY. Progress made by States and Union Territories is regularly updated through the PMAGY Portal.

The House was also informed that, across the country, 3,28,131 development works and 1,10,51,213 beneficiaries have been identified under the scheme. Of these, 46,642 development works have been completed, while 47,59,399 beneficiaries have already been saturated through various interventions.

With regard to Telangana, the written reply stated that under the education sector, 3,529 beneficiaries have been identified, of whom 472 beneficiaries have already received benefits under the scheme.

Replying to a query regarding third-party audit, Shri Athawale informed that States and Union Territories have been directed to verify the self-declaration of Adarsh Gram villages under the PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component. Accordingly, validation is being undertaken by the respective State and UT Governments.

The PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component continues to promote inclusive and sustainable rural development by improving access to education, infrastructure, livelihoods and essential services, thereby contributing to the socio-economic empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities across the country.

PR-048-TAR/KV/GA

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted through its appointed agency across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA, during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). The performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, captured during IDT are published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc.

These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Bhopal. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

The drive tests conducted across City drive – 292.3 KMs, Hotspot locations - 7, Walk Test - 1.4 KMs, in Haridwar and Rishikesh Cities & nearby areas during 29th June 2026 to 1st July 2026 in UP West LSA.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

 

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence (Mute) Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence (Mute) Instance: Number of call silence (Mute) instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

 

The overall mobile network performance in Haridwar and Rishikesh city for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

a)         Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1534/ 50508 for Airtel, 3920/ 49983 for BSNL, 2699/ 50069 for RJIL and 952/ 50338 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

 

b)         Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 10/ 430 for Airtel, 13/ 426 for BSNL, 2/ 453 for RJIL and 0/ 451 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

 

c)         Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 9/ 414 for Airtel, 21/ 408 for BSNL, 18/ 435 for RJIL and 12/ 451 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

 

d)         Data Download and Upload Throughput:

 

i)          Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 128.99 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 7.96 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 205.57 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 58.46 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

 

ii)         Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 24.54 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 4.11 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 23.21 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 14.79 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: -

  1. City - The areas covered in the city drive are Doiwala, Jolly Grant, Rishikesh, Tapovan, Veerbhadra, Nepali Farm, Raiwala, Haridwar, Jwalapur, Bahadrabad, Salempur Mahdood, Devpura, Ranipur and Sitapur etc. in Haridwar & Rishikesh city.
  2. Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are District Collectorate Office - Haridwar, Gurukul Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Haridwar Railway Station, Jolly Grant Airport - Dehradun, Raiwala Junction Railway Station, Rishikesh Bus Stand, Yog Nagari Rishikesh Railway Station.
  3. Walk Test - The walk tests conducted on 29th June & 1st July 2026, covered Har Ki Pauri Ganga Ghat - Haridwar, Triveni Ganga Ghat – Rishikesh capturing mobile network behaviour in crowded pedestrian environments.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs’ for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in  For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.bhopal@trai.gov.in or regional office of TRAI at Bhopal RO can be contacted on Phone no. +91-755-2575501

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries
“Quality Statistics as Driver of Change”
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

PRESS RELEASE- Day 1

The two-day meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSO) of BRICS Member Countries was inaugurated under the Chairship of India on 03 August 2026, at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India. The event brought together more than 350 participants including representatives from National Statistical Offices of BRICS, policy makers, academia, think-tanks, civil society organisation and technical experts.

 

2.         Guided under the overarching theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability (BRICS), the BRICS Statistics track, India has adopted the theme "Quality Statistics as Driver of Change”, reflecting an unwavering commitment to data quality, innovation, effective dissemination, and people-centric statistical systems that are responsive to rapid technological advancements, the growing demand for high-frequency and granular data, and the increasing reliance on official statistics to support evidence-based, sustainable, and inclusive development.

3.         The inaugural session of the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices was initiated with an introduction by DG (Data Governance), MoSPI followed by an address by Shri Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary, Planning and Programme Implementation, Uttar Pradesh.

4.         Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI and Chair of BRICS 2026 Statistics Track welcomed the delegates to the two-day event and highlighted key priorities of the BRICS Statistics Track 2026 centered on "Quality Statistics as a Driver of Change” including modernizing national statistical systems, utilizing administrative data and digital public infrastructure, and enhancing data governance and privacy standards. He also emphasised that, through technical exchanges and shared experiences, BRICS member nations aim to bridge data gaps, drive evidence-based decision-making, and build resilient statistical systems for the future.

5.         During the inaugural session, Heads of NSOs and representatives of BRICS member countries of Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) also shared brief introductions and their expectations from the meeting. The participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation under the BRICS Statistics Track and underscored the importance of international collaboration in advancing official statistics. They emphasised that sustained cooperation through knowledge sharing, exchange of best practices, harmonisation of statistical methodologies, and promotion of statistical innovation would enable BRICS Statistical community to strengthen the evidence base for informed policymaking, foster resilient economies, and accelerate progress towards sustainable development.

6.         A draft BRICS Joint Statistical Publication (JSP), 2026 and Snapshot BRICS JSP 2026 were released on August 3, 2026 during the meeting.  Any additional inputs or comments from BRICS member countries shall be incorporated subject to consensus of BRICS member countries.

7.         The BRICS Main Technical Session-I, titled "From Digital Platforms to Execution-Level Experience: National Practices and Strategic Approaches for Data Dissemination," featured presentations by different member countries, namely India, Brazil, China, Egypt, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and UAE. The presentations showcased national experiences, innovative approaches, and strategic initiatives aimed at strengthening data dissemination systems, enhancing accessibility, and promoting the effective use of official statistics in the digital era.

8.         The Technical Session-II on "Transformational Reforms in Statistical System" featured presentations by India, Ethiopia, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), highlighting national reforms, institutional innovations, and strategies to modernise statistical systems in response to the rapidly evolving data ecosystem.

9.         Besides the Technical sessions, a side-event on the theme, ‘Unlocking the potential of Administrative Data’ was also held on August 03, 2026 in collaboration with knowledge partner CivicDataLab, which was attended by representatives from BRICS member countries, civil society organizations, academia and officers from Central and State Governments.  The session highlighted the growing role of administrative data as a strategic national resource for producing more timely, cost-effective, and granular official statistics, while emphasising the need for harmonised metadata, interoperable systems, and stronger institutional collaboration. The discussions concluded with a call for stronger collaboration among governments, National Statistical Offices, academia, and technology partners to build trusted data ecosystems and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR–CRRI Flags Off Indigenous Network Survey Vehicle for Urban Road Monitoring; Launches Field Survey for CAQM-Supported Standard Framework Project in Delhi NCR
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

CSIR–Central Road Research Institute (CSIR–CRRI), New Delhi, today marked another significant milestone in advancing sustainable urban road infrastructure with the flag-off of the newly procured Indigenous Network Survey Vehicle (NSV) by Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR–CRRI. The event also marked the commencement of field surveys under the project titled "Implementation of the Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads in Delhi NCR."

The flag-off ceremony was held at the CSIR–CRRI Main Building by and attended by Dr.Ch.Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI and Dr.Thallada Bhaskar, Director, CSIR-AMPRI, Bhopal and HoDs, senior scientists, officials, engineers and staff members of the Institute. The newly inducted Network Survey Vehicle will be deployed for comprehensive condition assessment of urban roads across Delhi NCR, providing scientific, accurate and data-driven inputs for road asset management and sustainable urban infrastructure planning.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. C. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR–CRRI, stated that the deployment of the indigenous Network Survey Vehicle reflects CSIR–CRRI's commitment to developing and deploying advanced technologies for smarter and more sustainable road infrastructure. He emphasized that scientific assessment of existing road conditions is essential for planning durable pavements, improving mobility, reducing maintenance costs and supporting environmentally responsible urban development.

The field survey forms an important component of the project "Implementation of the Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads in Delhi NCR," being implemented by CSIR–CRRI in collaboration with the Public Works Department (PWD), Government of NCT of Delhi, under a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA). The project is being undertaken in accordance with the framework of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) for improving urban road infrastructure and mitigating dust pollution across the National Capital Region. This initiative forms part of a larger effort to implement the CAQM framework across NCR states. Under the project, CSIR-CRRI and SPA New Delhi will jointly undertake activities covering four major work packages: development of space standards and road cross-sections, mitigation of road dust through greening measures within the right-of-way, implementation of Road Asset Management Systems (RAMS) for improved maintenance practices, and promotion of innovative technologies for road construction.

The Network Survey Vehicle integrates state-of-the-art technologies, including high-speed laser profiling, UHD imaging systems, GPS/GNSS positioning, automated pavement distress mapping and AI-enabled data analytics. These capabilities enable rapid, non-contact assessment of pavement condition, road roughness, surface distress, drainage, shoulders and roadside assets while minimizing traffic disruption.

The data generated through the surveys will support scientific prioritization of maintenance works, standardized pavement design, improved drainage planning, enhanced road safety and effective monitoring of road conditions. The project is expected to contribute significantly towards reducing fugitive dust emissions, improving pavement quality and promoting sustainable urban mobility in Delhi NCR.

The event concluded with the formal flag-off of the Network Survey Vehicle and the launch of the field survey campaign, reaffirming CSIR–CRRI's leadership in providing innovative scientific solutions for national infrastructure development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
CDS Addresses Participants at the Fourth Edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Fourth Edition of the Tri-Services Future Warfare Course commenced at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi on August 03, 2026, with the Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS), General N.S. Raja Subramani, delivering the keynote address at the inaugural session.

In his address, the CDS focused on the changing character of warfare and the growing influence of emerging technologies on military operations. He emphasised the importance of anticipating future security challenges and developing the ability to respond effectively across multiple operational domains.

The CDS highlighted the increasing role of artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities, autonomous systems, information warfare, space technologies and data-driven decision-making in shaping future conflicts. He also stressed the need for greater jointness, integration and collaboration between the Armed Forces, industry, academia and the research community to strengthen national defence preparedness.

Conducted by the Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), this four-week course will bring together officers from the three Services along with representatives from government, industry, academia and strategic institutions. During the programme, participants will deliberate on subjects covering geopolitics, emerging technologies, cognitive and cyber warfare, multi-domain operations, scenario-building and technology-enabled warfare.

 

 

*********

 SR/ Kamlesh

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
EVALUATIONS OF MEASURABLE OUTCOMES DELIVERED BY SCM
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog in its report titled ‘Evaluation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes in Package 4 – Urban Transformation and Skill Development’ published in September 2025, has concluded that the Smart Cities Mission demonstrates strong alignment with national urban priorities and citizen needs, contributing significantly to multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. As per the report, the Mission has achieved a high project completion rate of 93% of 8,063 projects and 100% completion of Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs), leading to measurable improvements in urban liveability, mobility, safety, and environmental outcomes.

Under Smart Cities Mission (SCM), as reported by the States/UTs as on 31.03.2026, a total 8,064 projects amounting to ₹1,64,811 Cr were taken up out of which 7,790 projects (97% of total projects undertaken) worth ₹1,56,257 Cr have been completed. The key achievements and transformative outcomes of SCM inter-alia includes:

    1. 100 ICCCs established for functions spanning crime monitoring, citizen safety, transport, waste, water, and disaster management
    2. Public Safety and Security: More than 83,000 CCTV surveillance cameras installed
    3. Vibrant Public Spaces:1,300+ public-space projects completed, along with conservation of 484 heritage sites and market redevelopments in 58 cities
    4. Water Supply:17,000+ km of water supply network monitored via SCADA, reducing leakages and non-revenue water
    5. Solid Waste Management: ICCCs monitor RFID-enabled waste-collection vehicles, improving routes and collection efficiency
    6. Mobility:1,700+ km of smart, accessible roads built, with ITMS deployed and monitored via ICCCs for better traffic management
    7. Public Private Partnership (PPP): 194 projects worth ₹9,190 Cr with have been completed.

Post closure of SCM on 31.03.2025, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has issued Advisory No. 27 dated 10th June, 2025 to all States/ UTs. As per the advisory, the Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) are to ensure the timely completion of all ongoing SCM projects and prepare O&M plans for the assets created. The Advisory has further outlined the envisioned future role of SPVs of smart cities and a roadmap for the continued functioning of ICCCs.  The advisory underscores repurposing of SPVs to meet emerging urban challenges. 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
CLIMATE RESILIENT CITIES & URBAN HEATWAVES
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

As per the 12th Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban planning falls within the purview of the State Governments and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/Urban Development Authorities at the city level. Government of India supplements the efforts of States through schematic interventions, advisories, guidelines, financial assistance and technical support for strengthening the urban planning ecosystem.

As per inputs received, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has formulated 'National Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan-Prevention and Management of Heat Wave' in 2019. As per the guidelines, cities should carry out vulnerable assessments to identify major factors contributing to urban heat island effect and include suitable mitigation measures in their Heat Action Plans (HAPs). Heat Action Plans (HAPs) have been prepared by 23 states, 195 districts and 64 cities.

Further, National Disaster Management Authority has issued an advisory on “Protecting Informal Workers during Heatwaves in Indian Cities”. The Advisory outlines measures relating to health, safety and gender-sensitive adaptation. States and Union Territories have been  recommended to incorporate the needs of street vendors and other outdoor workers into Heat Action Plans through measures such as shaded vending zones, hydration facilities, cooling centers, flexible working hours and timely dissemination of heat alerts - https://ndma.gov.in/sites/default/files/PDF/Reports/NDMA_Advisory_for_Protecting_Informal_Workers_during_Heatwave.pdf

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) promotes climate-responsive and heat-resilient urban development through planning guidelines, technical advisories, and various urban development programmes. MoHUA has issued the Urban Green Guidelines, 2014 and the Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, 2014, which encourage compact and green urban development, green infrastructure, urban forest, conservation of water bodies, shaded public spaces, and other planning measures to mitigate urban heat stress.

Further, the URDPFI Guidelines, 2014, under Chapter 5 – Urban Planning Approach–  encourage climate-responsive planning, energy-efficient building design, green infrastructure, and environmentally sustainable development practices, while recommending that States/UTs incorporate such provisions in their planning and development regulations.

Since urban planning and development are State subjects, implementation of cool roof measures, green building provisions, and related building regulations is undertaken by the respective State Governments/Urban Local Bodies in accordance with local planning and building bye-laws.

Under PMAY-U, MoHUA supplements the efforts of States/UTs, by providing Central Assistance for pucca houses to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country since 25.06.2015. Under PMAY-U, a Technology Sub-Mission (TSM) was set up to facilitate adoption of modern, innovative and green technologies and building material for faster and quality construction of houses. Building upon progress of TSM, Technology & Innovation Sub-Mission(TISM) supports innovative design and construction practices, promote quality assurance and adopting green building standards for sustainable housing in the country. Projects under the Mission encourage use of resource-efficient, climate-responsive, disaster-resilient and eco-friendly materials and technologies, in line with prevailing green building norms to enhance thermal comfort, reduce energy consumption and minimize environmental impact.

As per inputs from Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP) released by MoEFCC, provides an integrated vision for sustainable cooling across sectors including transport with the overarching goal of providing sustainable cooling and thermal comfort socio-economic benefits. Specific Action Points for the transport sector thematic area have been finalized after mapping the recommendations with the concerned government schemes/activities. It mainly provides for (a) Adoption of the Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC) norms in the development of new and existing public transport infrastructure viz. railway stations, airports, ports etc.; (b) Promotion of research and development for transition to low Global Warming Potential (GWP) refrigerants and energy efficient Mobile Air-Conditioning (MAC) systems; (c) Upskilling of service technicians in the MAC sector; (d) Environmentally sound management and recovery of refrigerants from end-of-life vehicles and during servicing operations, etc.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme
Churning the Ocean for Energy
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

Samudra Manthan marks a decisive step in India's journey towards energy security and self-reliance. With a Phase-I outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030–31, the scheme is designed to unlock India's vast offshore hydrocarbon potential. It focuses on accelerating exploration, deploying modern technology, creating shared infrastructure, and strengthening domestic manufacturing. It aims to add over 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, raise domestic production, reduce import dependence, and build a globally competitive offshore energy ecosystem.

 

 A New Chapter in Offshore Exploration

Energy powers every aspect of modern life. It fuels homes, farms, industries, transport, and the wider economy. As India continues its rapid growth, ensuring a reliable, affordable, and secure energy supply has become a national priority. While the country's energy needs continue to rise, a significant share of its crude oil and natural gas requirements is met through imports. Expanding domestic production is therefore essential to strengthen energy security, reduce import dependence, and conserve valuable foreign exchange.

Among the country's key energy resources are hydrocarbons—organic compounds made of hydrogen and carbon. They occur deep below the land and the seabed. Crude oil and natural gas are the widely used hydrocarbons. They provide the raw material for petrol, diesel, LPG, petrochemicals, fertilisers, and numerous industrial products.

India's offshore basins hold vast untapped hydrocarbon potential. A basin is a large natural depression in the earth where hydrocarbons collect.  Unlocking these resources requires modern exploration, reliable geological data, advanced drilling capabilities, and a strong domestic supply chain. To accelerate this effort, Samudra Manthan – the National Offshore Exploration Scheme has been approved on 31 July 2026. With a Phase-I outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030‑31, it aims to boost the hydrocarbon exploration and production sector.

 Why The Seas Hold the Key for India

India is the world’s third-largest consumer of crude oil. Its annual import bill is nearly USD 144 billion, or about ₹13 lakh crore. Recent global events have shown how vital uninterrupted energy access is. Higher domestic output has thus become critical for a rapidly growing economy.

The Offshore Opportunity

Much of India’s future oil and gas potential lies offshore. Deepwater and ultra-deepwater basins are sea zones with very high-water depth. India’s eastern and western offshore basins extend to water depths of up to 3,000 metres. They are estimated to hold over 5,600 MMTOE (Million Metric Tonnes of Oil Equivalent) of hydrocarbon potential. Recent finds in the Cauvery, Mahanadi, and Andaman basins have reinforced this promise.

ONGC's Fixed Offshore Platform

The Challenge of Deepwater Exploration

Exploration is a costly and patient activity. Moving from the award of an exploration block to commercial production typically takes 5–10 years. A single deepwater exploratory well costs about USD 125–150 million. Such high stakes can discourage offshore exploration.

There is another reason why constant search matters. Existing fields witness a natural decline of around 6–7 percent every year. New discoveries are needed simply to sustain current output. Sustained exploration thus serves as a path to lasting self-reliance in energy.

 Inside the Samudra Manthan Mission

Samudra Manthan marks the transition from policy reform to mission-mode implementation. The scheme adopts a risk-sharing approach to attract sustained investment into frontier waters. It seeks to de-risk offshore ventures and encourage private capital, building enduring national capability across the value chain. In doing so, it converts a decade of reform into concrete action at sea.

Components of Samudra Manthan

Offshore exploration depends on reliable data, advanced technology, modern infrastructure, and a resilient supply chain. Samudra Manthan brings these elements together through four components.

  1. Seismic Data Acquisition, Processing, and Interpretation

Limited offshore seismic coverage restricted the identification of drill-ready oil and gas prospects. The scheme funds large-scale 2D and 3D seismic surveys with an outlay of ₹28,534 crore. Advanced technology and Artificial Intelligence will speed up processing and interpretation. Older data in the National Data Repository will also be re-processed with modern tools.

  1. Accelerated Offshore Exploration

High cost and long gestation make deepwater drilling a risky venture. To share this risk, the scheme allocates ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells. Financial support covers up to 50 percent of eligible drilling cost, or ₹675 crore per well, whichever is lower. The scheme is open to both public and private Exploration and Production (E&P) operators to increase oil and gas reserves. It will accelerate reserve accretion and unlock India’s deepwater potential.

  1. Common Offshore Infrastructure

Many offshore discoveries remain unproduced due to costly infrastructure, particularly in the Mahanadi and Kutch basins. The scheme provides ₹10,000 crore for shared production and evacuation facilities in select basins. Common infrastructure lowers project costs and turns idle finds into producing fields.

  1. Oil and Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone

Low domestic manufacturing increases exploration costs, import dependence, and foreign exchange outflow. In view of this, an integrated Oil and Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone will be established with ₹2,000 crore. It will build domestic capabilities in manufacturing, repair, warehousing, engineering, and services. This directly advances Make in India across the supply chain. An amount of ₹350 crore supports monitoring, digital interventions, evaluation, human resources, awareness and outreach, events, and media.

An Integrated Enabling Ecosystem

Beyond funding, the scheme creates a supportive environment for the entire value chain. Dedicated provisions cover:

  • Digital programme management for transparent and efficient implementation
  • Capacity building for professionals across the sector
  • Adoption of cutting-edge technologies
  • Continuous stakeholder engagement
  • International outreach to attract global partners

 What Samudra Manthan Will Deliver

The scheme is designed to create value for the economy and future generations. Subject to exploration success, it is expected to bring wide-ranging gains:

  • Larger Reserves: Increase of over 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, expanding the resource base from 1.6 billion to 2.2 billion Tonnes of Oil Equivalent (TOE).
  • Higher Output: Annual domestic production is targeted to rise from around 62 MMTOE to 80 MMTOE. Incremental production of 10–15 MMTOE is expected, with a peak potential of 20 MMTOE.
  • Lower Import Bill: Additional output can cut crude imports by nearly ₹1 lakh crore every year, generating significant foreign exchange savings.
  • Investment and Growth: The scheme will promote investments across the value chain and drive strong GDP expansion.
  • Employment: Large-scale jobs will be created in exploration, production, and allied activities.
  • Indigenous Strength: Domestic manufacturing will deepen under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, fostering a globally competitive ecosystem for offshore technologies.

Together, these outcomes strengthen the country’s energy resilience. They also nurture technological leadership and long-term opportunities for industry and innovation.

A Series of Reforms

In recent years, India has steadily rebuilt its hydrocarbon exploration and production ecosystem. A series of structural reforms has made the sector open, transparent, and investor-friendly.

  • Opening Up Offshore Acreage: More than 99 percent of the earlier “No-Go” areas have been removed. Over one million square kilometres of the Exclusive Economic Zone is now available for exploration. This zone is the sea area where India holds rights over natural resources.
  • New Licensing Framework: The Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) was launched in 2016. Under it the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP) was launched which replaced the old nomination-based approach. HELP provides lower levies, uniform licensing, revenue sharing, and incentives to promote hydrocarbon exploration and early production.
  • Simpler Contracts: India moved from Production Sharing Contracts (PSC) to Revenue Sharing Contracts (RSC) in 2016. In PSC, profits were shared between the Government and the contractor after recovery of cost. In RSC, the contractor bears all exploration risks, production and development costs in return for its stipulated share of revenue. Thus, this fiscal framework became simpler and more transparent, with less administrative intervention.
  • Modern Law: The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025 provided contractual stability and stronger dispute resolution. It recognised integrated petroleum operations and created a contemporary regulatory architecture.
  • Enabling Rules: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025 operationalised these changes. They promote ease of doing business and streamline the administration of petroleum leases.
  • Level Playing Field: The composition and mandate of the Empowered Committee of Secretaries were standardised across all contract regimes. Every operator now enjoys consistent treatment, whenever their contract was signed.
  • Sharper Focus: The performance parameters of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India were reoriented towards exploration. This reinforces the national commitment to expanding the domestic resource base.

Good exploration begins with good data. Seismic surveys send sound waves into the earth to map rock layers below the seabed. India has made sustained investments in such geoscientific knowledge through several national initiatives. These include Mission Anveshan, the National Seismic Programme, the Extended Continental Shelf Survey, the National Data Repository, and the Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study. Together, these have created one of the world’s most comprehensive geoscientific databases.

The reforms have inspired visible confidence. Nearly 81 percent of active exploration acreage has been awarded after 2014. Under OALP, 172 blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh square kilometres have been awarded. Committed investments in these blocks exceed USD 4.3 billion. Activity on the ground has gathered pace as well. During FY 2025‑26 alone, around 674 wells were drilled. Five new discoveries were made and seven discoveries were monetised.

 

A New Chapter Begins in the Mahanadi Basin

The hydrocarbon exploration reform journey reached a proud moment on 25 July 2026. Drilling of the first appraisal well commenced in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin. An appraisal well is drilled to further evaluate the quality and commercial value of the hydrocarbon discovery. The programme will deploy world-class deepwater drilling technology. The MN-DWN18-1-HD well is the first of four planned deepwater wells. These wells will systematically evaluate one of India’s most prospective offshore basins.

The spudding (start of drilling a new well) marks the beginning of one of India’s most challenging deepwater campaigns. Every prospect evaluated and every well drilled will take the nation closer to self-reliance.

 

Towards a Secure Energy Future

India stands at the threshold of a promising energy era. The nation’s energy future doesn’t rest on a single discovery. It is being built through sustained reform, science, and the dedication of thousands of geologists, engineers, and offshore professionals.

Samudra Manthan blends data, shared risk, common facilities, and homegrown capability into one mission. As the churn of the ocean begins, it carries the aspirations of a rising nation. Each step taken beneath the waves brings the country closer to a secure and self-reliant tomorrow.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India’s two-week Online Short -Term Internship Programme begins
100 university-level students from diverse academic backgrounds shortlisted out of 2,036 applicants
Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian highlights rising global conflicts, calls for greater empathy among youth
Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi holds right to life with dignity a fundamental right and urges interns to promote human rights in society
Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal urges interns to become conscientious citizens committed to human rights
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

 

The two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme (OSTI) organised by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India for university-level students began at Manav Adhikar Bhawan, New Delhi today. NHRC Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian inaugurated the programme in the presence of Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi; Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal; Joint Secretaries, Shri Samir Kumar, Smt. Saidingpuii Chhakchhuak and Director, Ms. Satovisha Samajdar. 100 students from diverse academic backgrounds, selected from 2,036 applicants, are participating in the programme.

Addressing them, Justice Ramasubramanian said that the youth in the country are fortunate to live away from conflict happening in different parts of the world. They have access to basic human rights such as food, education and shelter unlike several people facing armed conflicts and displacement. Citing the Global Peace Index 2025, released by the Institute for Economics and Peace, he said that the world is currently facing an estimated 130-armed conflicts, the highest since World War II. 98 countries are facing external conflicts and over 122 million people have been forcibly displaced. The global economic damage has reached nearly USD 20 trillion, highlighting the serious humanitarian situation across the world.

Justice Ramasubramanian described the internship programme as an effective way to engage and sensitise young people about the importance of human rights. They evolve as brand ambassadors of the Commission. He emphasised that the purpose of the NHRC internship programme is to foster empathy and compassion towards fellow human beings. He said that the programme would be successful if it could strengthen these values among the participants, even by one per cent. He urged them to make the best use of the opportunity.

 

NHRC Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi said that the internship programme has been structured to provide valuable learning on various aspects of human rights through lectures by eminent subject experts. Referring to Article 21 of the Constitution of India, he said that the right to life with dignity is a fundamental right and encouraged the interns to use the knowledge gained through the programme for their benefit and that of society.

 

Earlier, Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal said that the online format makes the internship programme more inclusive and accessible by removing geographical and financial barriers, enabling students from across the country to participate. He said that over the next two weeks, the interns would interact with eminent speakers, gaining a deeper understanding of the mandate and functioning of the NHRC. He added that the internship aims to inspire them to become conscientious citizens who uphold the dignity of fellow human beings and work to protect the rights of people around them. He expressed the hope that the internship will enrich their understanding of human rights and inspire them to carry forward the values of justice, equality and human dignity in their academic, professional and personal lives.

Joint Secretary, Smt. Saidingpuii Chhakchhuak presented an overview of the two-week internship programme. The programme will feature around 30 lectures on important human rights topics and involve 20 eminent guest speakers, including senior government officials, academicians, civil society representatives, human rights defenders, NHRC officers, representatives from international institutions working for the protection of human rights and subject experts. The interns will be given virtual tours of a Police Station, Tihar Prison and Asha Kiran Shelter Home to understand their functioning and challenges, besides participating in a book review competition, group research project presentation and declamation contest.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia to convene Investors’ Meet along with MP CM Mohan Yadav to attract Investment for Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior
India’s First TMZ eyes ₹10,000 Crore in Investments; Mumbai Investors’ Meet Set to Accelerate Investment Momentum
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai : 3 August 2026

Building on the momentum of the launch of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Jyotiraditya M. Scindia will convene a Telecom Manufacturing Zone Investors Meet in Mumbai on 4 August 2026 along with the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Mohan Yadav; Secretary of Department of Telecom, Amit Agarwal and Additional Chief Secretary, Madhya Pradesh Govt., Neeraj Mandloi. The first roadshow and the Investors’ Meet in Mumbai comes close on the heels of the landmark launch of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July 2026. 

The TMZ launch was followed by the first Investors’ Roundtable in the national capital. Minister Scindia announced investment commitments of ₹3,500 crore were secured with the potential to generate nearly 14,000 employment opportunities, reflecting the strong confidence of industry in India’s growing telecom manufacturing ecosystem. The Mumbai Investors’ Meet and roadshow marks the next phase of this national initiative to mobilise greater industry participation and investments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone. It will bring together leading telecom manufacturers, technology companies, infrastructure providers, component manufacturers and investors to accelerate the development of a world-class telecom manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The expected investment in India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is expected to cross ₹10,000 Crore mark. 

The establishment of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a landmark stride towards realising the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector. By creating an integrated ecosystem for manufacturing, research and development, design, testing and innovation, the TMZ aims to strengthen domestic value chains, reduce import dependence, promote indigenous manufacturing, boost exports and position India as a trusted global hub for telecom products and next-generation technologies.

The enthusiastic response from industry at the inaugural Investors’ Roundtable underscored the transformative potential of the initiative. Leading companies and several telecom industry leaders, committed significant investments towards the project, reaffirming their confidence in India’s policy framework and manufacturing capabilities.

The Mumbai Investors’ Meet is expected to further deepen industry partnerships and attract fresh investments, reinforcing the Government’s commitment to building a globally competitive telecom manufacturing ecosystem and transforming India into a leading global destination for telecom manufacturing and innovation.

The event will bring together senior government officials, industry leaders, investors and key stakeholders from the telecommunications sector.


PIB Mumbai | Nikita Joshi/ Yash Rané/ Priti Malandkar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship Observes Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 with Enthusiastic Participation Across the Country
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) successfully observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16th July to 31st July 2026, reaffirming its commitment towards the vision of Swachh Bharat Mission and promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental sustainability across all its offices, attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and field institutions.

The Swachhata Pakhwada was organised in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. During the fortnight, a wide range of activities were undertaken throughout the Ministry and its organisations to foster awareness and encourage active participation among officers, officials, trainees and stakeholders.

The observance commenced with the Swachhata Pledge administered by Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary (MSDE), where in officers and staﬀ reaffirmed their commitment towards maintaining cleanliness and promoting hygienic practices in their workplaces and surroundings.

As part of the awareness initiatives, the Ministry organised various employee engagement activities including a Poster Making Competition and Slogan Writing Competition on the theme of cleanliness and environmental conservation. A workshop on "Curbing Single-use Plastic" was also organised to sensitise participants about sustainable alternatives and responsible waste management practices.

In addition to above, tree plantation drive was also organised in Kaushal Bhawan. Saplings of indigenous tree species were planted by the all the senior officers to promote environmental conservation, enhance green cover and reinforce the message of sustainable development. The initiative reflected the Ministry's commitment towards fostering a cleaner, greener and environmentally responsible ecosystem.

Addressing the occasion, senior officers of the Ministry emphasised that cleanliness is a shared responsibility and an essential component of creating safe, healthy and productive workplaces. They encouraged all employees and trainees to adopt cleanliness as a way of life and continue practising the principles of Swachhata beyond the Pakhwada.

MSDE's attached offices, subordinate offices, autonomous bodies, and other training institutions actively participated in the campaign by organising plantation drives, awareness programmes, community outreach activities, cleanliness campaigns and behavioural change initiatives in collaboration with local communities.

The Ministry also undertook extensive digital outreach through its official website and social media platforms by disseminating messages promoting cleanliness, sustainable practices and citizen participation in the Swachh Bharat Mission.

The Ministry expressed its appreciation to all attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and field institutions for their enthusiastic participation and successful implementation of the activities under Swachhata Pakhwada 2026. The collective efforts demonstrated during the fortnight reflect MSDE's continued commitment towards building a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

item.title: PRADHAN MANTRI SHRAM YOGI MAANDHAN (PM-SYM)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
PRADHAN MANTRI SHRAM YOGI MAANDHAN (PM-SYM)
Over 54 Lakh Beneficiaries Enrolled Under PM-SYM Across the Country
Posted On: 03 AUG 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) scheme was launched in February, 2019 in order to provide old age protection to the workers of the unorganised sector. This is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme. Under the scheme, a monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/- is provided to the unorganised workers after attaining the age of 60 years. The workers in the age group of 18 to 40 years whose monthly income is Rs. 15000/- or less and not a member of Employees Provident Fund Organization (EPFO)/Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)/National Pension System (NPS) (Contributed by Central Govt.) or not an income tax assessee are eligible to join the scheme. The monthly contribution amount ranges from Rs. 55/- to Rs. 200/-, depending upon the entry age of the beneficiary. Under the scheme, 50% monthly contribution is payable by the beneficiary and equal matching contribution is paid by the Central Government. Enrolment in the Scheme is done through the Common Service Centres, with its network of about 4 lakh Centres across the country. Eligible unorganised workers can also self-enrol through visiting the portal www.maandhan.in.

As on 29.07.2026, more than 54 lakh beneficiaries have been enrolled under the PM-SYM scheme across the country. The participation of women unorganised workers in this scheme is 53.1%. The 50 percent matching contribution of the Government under the PM-SYM Scheme across the country is Rs. 2,011.01 crore. Further, pension to the beneficiaries will start after attaining the age of 60 years. Since the scheme was launched in February, 2019, the disbursement of pension will start not before February, 2039.

Under the PM-SYM Scheme, subscriber accounts may become inactive primarily due to non-payment of the prescribed monthly contribution, which may occur on account of insufficient balance in the subscriber's bank account, change or closure of the linked bank account, or lack of continued awareness regarding regular contributions.

The steps taken by the Government to improve retention, increase participation and increase awareness are as under:

(i) Holding periodic review meetings with States/UTs.

(ii) Providing incentives to Common Services Centres (CSCs) for enrolling eligible beneficiaries under the PM-SYM scheme.

(iii) Launch of new features such as Voluntary Exit, Revival Module, Claim Status and Account Statement.

(iv) Extension of the revival period of dormant accounts from one year to three years.

(v) Two-way integration of PM-SYM with eShram portal.

(vi) Conducting SMS campaigns for awareness generation.

(vii) Addressing Chief Secretaries of States/UTs regarding enrollment under the PM-SYM Scheme.

(viii) Organize nationwide special registration drive for enrolment of unorganised workers under the scheme.

This information was given by the Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
